A temporal convolutional network (TCN) used 180 min of history, constrained during training by a personalized four-parameter physiological model. The main PMB--NN combined forecast and neural--physiological agreement losses; a three-term variant additionally fitted physiological predictions to measured glucose. Data comprised 6--8 weeks of continuous glucose monitoring, pump, and meal records from 25 AZT1D participants. Person-specific models used chronological 70/10/20 train/validation/test splits and 30-, 60-, and 120-min horizons. Median mean absolute errors were 16.24, 25.00, and 30.20 mg/dL with basal insulin records and 15.38, 24.21, and 31.79 mg/dL before these records became available. In the latter setting, PMB--NN had the lowest median error at 30 and 60 min; it outperformed the physiological model alone in all six settings. In input-increase tests, glucose predictions changed in the expected direction for 85\% of correction boluses and 100\% of carbohydrate rescues, versus 57\% for active insulin and 56\% for active carbohydrates. Most standalone physiological fits showed locally distinguishable parameter effects, with glucose-related coefficients more stable under resampling than insulin- or carbohydrate-related coefficients. The three-term variant improved hyperglycaemia accuracy with basal records, but did not significantly change overall MAE and reduced directional plausibility in three tests. PMB--NN combines personalized forecasting with an explicit physiological model, allowing assessment of predictive accuracy, physiological response behavior, and participant-specific coefficients.

items.title: Hyperbolic dynamic friction models for viscoelastic sliding and rolling contact
items.summary: This paper considers the sliding and rolling contact between viscoelastic bodies. Combining linear viscoelastic rheologies for bristle-like elements with nonlinear dynamic friction models, and under the assumption of small deformations and displacement gradients, it derives a class of viscoelasto-kinematic equations, formulated as a system of semilinear partial differential equations (PDEs) governing the evolution of the frictional force, bristle deformations, and internal state variables at the interface between the contacting bodies. The resulting system is analysed mathematically, demonstrating that linear viscoelasticity preserves the hyperbolic character of the PDE systems typically encountered in rolling contact. The proposed theory is illustrated through representative examples of both sliding and rolling contact, highlighting that these two processes, whilst often treated as distinct, may in fact exhibit closely related underlying dynamics. Overall, the framework provides a general theoretical setting applicable to a broad class of viscoelastic frictional systems.

items.title: Hierarchical universal open structure dataset for atomistic modeling
items.summary: Atomic-scale simulations have been transformed by machine-learning models that predict the properties of atomistic structures with the accuracy of quantum calculations, but at a small fraction of the cost. These models have increased dramatically in generality, thanks to the availability of synthetic datasets of ever-increasing size and scope. The proliferation of datasets, with properties often computed using different levels of electronic-structure approximation, is problematic, as there is often overlap between different datasets, and strong correlations between structures obtained with short molecular dynamics trajectories or geometry optimization. To address these problems, we introduce a protocol to stratify a dataset into a hierarchy of nested subsets, subsampling from the coarsest to the finest resolution based on an "ecumetric" built to reflect the latent space representation of several popular universal machine-learning interatomic potentials. We then use this approach to combine most of the open structural datasets currently available, consolidating them into MAD-COSMO, a well-organized collection of almost 1.7 billion structures, whose $2^{24}$ most diverse members form the MAD-CORE stratified coreset, which can be easily used for all sorts of tasks, from exploratory experiments to the training of foundation models at scale. We envision that this collection will guide and help coordinate future efforts, focusing them on the most relevant and/or undersampled regions of chemical and structural space, and that it will be further extended to incorporate the outcomes of the collective work of this community.

items.title: Lacunarity in a Two-Dimensional Atomizing Liquid Jet
items.summary: Atomization stretches and folds the liquid--gas interface before fragmenting it into ligaments and droplets, making fractal measures a natural descriptor of the lacunarity of the final breakup state. We examine this idea in two-dimensional (2D) VOF-DNS of a liquid jet with adaptive mesh refinement in Basilisk. Box-counting of the full resolved interface does not yield a single scale-independent exponent. Instead, two scaling ranges appear, separated by a crossover near the box-counting level \(L_{\mathrm{box}}\simeq7\): coarser boxes measure the folded connected jet envelope, whereas finer boxes increasingly sample ligaments, droplets, and nearly smooth local interface segments. Decomposing the interface into detached droplets, ligaments, and the connected main body shows that the relevant effective dimension is structure dependent. Droplets are most lacunar with dimension below one, ligaments occupy an intermediate level, and the main body carries the largest coarse-scale dimension. This hierarchy persists over $Re_l=100$--$10^4$ at fixed $\We_g=200$. The lacunarity of droplets is reminiscent of that of the object positions in the night sky hypothesized by de Vaucouleurs.

items.title: Watt-level single-cavity dual-comb laser at 2.1 $μ$m wavelength
items.summary: Compact ultrafast laser combs around the 2 $μ$m atmospheric transmission window are of growing interest for direct spectroscopy and as drivers for nonlinear conversion to otherwise hard-to-reach spectral regions. Dual-comb systems in this region remain very scarce: existing implementations rely mostly on nonlinear conversion, resulting in complex systems with poor conversion efficiency and overall low average and peak power. In this paper, we report on a watt-level dual-comb laser directly emitting at 2.1 $μ$m. The system is based on a single-cavity, soft-aperture Kerr-lens mode-locked (KLM) laser using a broadband holmium (Ho)-doped CaAlGdO$_4$ (CALGO) gain crystal. The laser delivers a total output power exceeding 2 W (1 W per comb) with a sub-100-fs pulse duration (50 nm bandwidth) at a repetition rate of 96.5 MHz, corresponding to a pulse energy of 10 nJ and a peak power of 100 kW per comb. To assess the source's potential for future spectroscopic applications, we characterize the free-running dual comb in detail for frequency stability, phase noise, and relative intensity noise (RIN), and benchmark the achievable spectral resolution by measuring spectral modulations imposed by Fabry-Pérot etalons. Our system combines the compactness, high efficiency, and passive mutual coherence of a single-cavity oscillator with watt-level average power at 2.1 $μ$m, making it a promising source for environmental sensing in the atmospheric transmission window, or as a driver for nonlinear frequency conversion, for example, to the MIR and THz regions.

items.title: Gas release from metals under irradiation with elliptic Gaussian laser beam during LID-QMS analysis
items.summary: Laser-induced-desorption quadrupole-mass-spectrometry (LID-QMS) diagnostics is considered as one of the candidate methods for the remote control of tritium inventory in the ITER first wall. Studies involving LID-QMS generally assume the circular shape of the laser spot on the analyzed surface. At the same time, the diagnostics laser source cannot be always positioned so as to irradiate tokamak tiles under normal angles, which results in the laser spot shape differing from the circular one. In this contribution, we analyze the tritium removal process under sample irradiation by an elliptic Gaussian laser beam, extending the results of our previous analysis [A.A. Stepanenko, Yu.M. Gasparyan, Physica Scripta 99 (8), 085604 (2025)]. The thermal desorption model governing the heat transport and tritium removal from the solid is formulated. The new analytical expression describing the sample temperature dynamics is derived. The developed model is used to examine the impact of the laser beam/spot ellipticity on the tritium desorption process from a tungsten sample. The conditions, under which the elliptic beam can be approximated with the circular one for the rapid assessment of the amount of desorbed tritium, are assessed.

items.title: Beam shifts and eigenpolarisations for the reflection of vortex beams from homogeneous magnetic surfaces
items.summary: Probing surfaces with optical beams is a powerful technique utilised for material characterisation, and more recently, measuring surface magnetisation with vortex beams has opened new avenues by utilising OAM beams for metrology. In this paper, we focus on extending the theoretical framework of unit order vortex beam reflection to spatially homogeneous magnetic surfaces, and derive expressions for the Goos-Hänchen (GH) and Imbert-Federov (IF) shifts. We calculate closed form expressions for the plane wave eigenpolarisations, polarisations which remain in the same vectorial direction after reflection, for both dielectric and homogeneous magnetic surfaces. These are found by extending the singularimetry formalism for dielectric surfaces, where the position of the phase vortex can be analytically approximated by taking into account the finite beam width, to homogeneous magnetic surfaces. From this we find the eigenpolarisations of the unit order vortex beam for reflection from both dielectric and homogeneous magnetic surfaces. We discuss with relation to the analytical forms of the Jones matrices for GH and IF shifts the additional reflection behaviour observed for homogeneous magnetic surfaces.

items.title: Modeling inhomogeneous spatial point configurations with applications to replicated patterns in real-life waiting crowds
items.summary: In this article, we connect statistical inference for spatial point processes with the analysis of waiting pedestrian crowds through two interconnected contributions. First, on the methodological side we develop an inference procedure for semiparametric spatial point process models leveraging replicated spatial patterns, i.e., multiple approximately independent realizations from the same process. Second, we show that spatial point processes provide a suitable modeling framework for waiting pedestrians, capturing two key aspects: spatial inhomogeneity driven by location attractiveness and repulsive interactions between pedestrians. These two components are central to the inference problem itself, since spatial point process modeling hinges on disentangling background intensity from interaction. Although replicated spatial patterns are rare in point process literature, they are available here through a unique real-life pedestrian dataset, thereby directly linking the methodological development to the physical application. We use the proposed methods to fit and evaluate determinantal and Gibbs point processes in a simulation study and a real-world case study. Despite persistent challenges in decoupling the influences of inhomogeneity from interaction, these models are able to reproduce key empirical features of waiting pedestrians.

items.title: Fairness, Travel, and Market Potential: An Optimization Framework for NBA Expansion
items.summary: The potential expansion of the National Basketball Association (NBA) to 32 teams raises the question of how to restructure its conferences and divisions while balancing travel efficiency, fairness in team travel burdens, and commercial exposure. This study provides a quantitative framework for expansion planning. We develop two optimization models: one minimizing total travel distance and another following the Kalai-Smorodinsky (KS) proportional-improvement principle. The KS model maximizes the smallest normalized travel improvement between a team's fixed reference and individual ideal. Both models incorporate an opponent-exposure constraint to account for commercial considerations, and take into account road trips when measuring travel distance. Using data from all 30 current franchises and six candidate cities (Seattle, Las Vegas, Montreal, Vancouver, Tampa, and Mexico City), we evaluate 15 pairwise expansion scenarios under alternative season lengths and divisional formats. In the 30-team comparison, KS strikes a good balance between overall travel efficiency and fairness across teams, giving greater attention to individual travel burdens while keeping total travel close to the distance-minimizing solution. The expansion results show that travel requirements depend jointly on the candidate city pair and the competition format, highlighting the need to assess expansion and realignment together. Our study offers a flexible decision support framework for league executives, policymakers, and sports economists. It makes the trade-offs between total travel, individual gains, and opponent exposure explicit, providing evidence-based guidance for strategic league design.

items.title: Correlation between normal character and Raman intensities of isotopologues of carbon dioxide
items.summary: Previous studies on the vibrational structure of carbon dioxide isotopologues have revealed a correlation between the strength of Fermi interactions and a recently defined normal-mode parameter. In this contribution, we investigate how the Raman intensities of the most intense bands evolve across the complete series of carbon dioxide isotopologues at room temperature. To this end, we introduce a general scheme for simulating Raman intensities in linear triatomic molecules, based on the computation of the mean polarizability surface up to cubic terms for all twelve stable species. For the first time, we establish correlations between the degree of normality and the Raman transition intensities, mean polarizability derivatives, and variational Raman shift errors across the CO$_2$ isotopologue series. The observed trends are further analyzed by considering rotational contributions, which may partially account for the deviations observed in the correlations. Our study is supported by experimental Raman spectra of isotopically enriched samples and theoretical simulations. Although this study focuses on carbon dioxide, similar behavior is expected for other series of isotopologues.

items.title: From Algebraic Completeness to Orbit Separation: Recursive Separating Invariants for Global Neural Network Potential Energy Surfaces
items.summary: Permutationally invariant polynomials (PIPs) provide a systematically improvable, symmetry-preserving representation for global potential energy surfaces (PESs), but their high computational cost as neural network descriptors limits applications to large molecular systems. Fundamental invariants (FIs), which form an algebraically complete generating set, substantially reduce the number of descriptors and enable neural network PESs for larger systems. However, PES evaluation remains computationally expensive as molecular size and complexity increase. Here, we introduce recursive separating invariants (RSIs), shifting the descriptor design principle from algebraic completeness to orbit separation. RSIs are constructed systematically through correlation order and recursion depth, providing a more computationally efficient representation. Benchmarks on reactive and nonreactive systems demonstrate that RSI-based neural network (RSI-NN) PESs achieve approximately an order-of-magnitude faster evaluation than their FI-NN counterparts, with system-dependent prediction accuracy that is comparable in several cases. These results establish orbit separation as a promising principle for developing efficient symmetry-preserving descriptors for global neural network PESs.

items.title: Thermal Confinement in Plasmonic Nanoparticles under Generalised Pulsed Illumination
items.summary: Thermal confinement is a key parameter in photothermal applications, as it determines the spatial extent of the region affected by the generated heat. In this work, we develop a numerical treatment to quantify thermal confinement in spherical plasmonic nanoparticles under excitation conditions ranging from ultrashort pulses to the continuous-wave regime. The model combines generalized optical heating with a finite-difference solution of the transient heat equation and explicitly accounts for finite interfacial thermal conductance. To characterize the spatial distribution of heat, we introduce a thermal confinement radius defined from the temporal temperature envelope in the surrounding medium. We demonstrate that pulse duration acts as a highly effective, tuneable parameter to govern thermal confinement. Notably, we quantitatively show that finite interfacial thermal conductance can induce deviations of up to 20% in the spatial confinement radius and over 60% in the transient thermal construct under ultrashort excitation. By comparing the characteristic dimensions of representative targeting ligands with the resulting thermal-confinement length scales, we show how pulse duration can be precisely tailored to control target heating. These results provide a unified framework for predicting nanoscale heat localization paving the way for the rational design of high precision thermoplasmonic applications.

items.title: Hurricane Laura-induced loads on wind turbines -- Part I: High-fidelity modeling and sensitivity to turbulent inflow conditions
items.summary: Tropical cyclones can produce extreme winds in the lowest portion of the boundary layer, posing high risks to critical energy infrastructure, including wind energy systems. This study evaluates the dynamic response of an idling wind turbine to turbulent inflow generated during the passage of a hurricane. We performed large-eddy simulations of Hurricane Laura (2020) at several grid resolutions -- coarse $(Δx=55.55\,{\rm m})$, intermediate $(Δx=25\,{\rm m})$, and fine $(Δx=10\,{\rm m})$ -- to investigate differences in mean flow characteristics and turbulence structures as the hurricane progresses across a virtual wind turbine location. The large-eddy simulation data served as direct inflow conditions for aeroelastic simulations to assess the turbine's response. Our results reveal significant differences in the mean wind and turbulent flow structures between the grid resolutions, leading to distinct impacts on the wind turbine's aeroelastic behavior. These findings emphasize the need for high-resolution inflow information to better predict extreme loads and inform the design of wind turbines in regions frequently affected by tropical cyclones. As a continuation of this work, Part II of this study will evaluate the turbine's response from different locations relative to the storm's trajectory and compare it with current wind turbine design practices.

items.title: Boltzmann generators for amorphous particle systems
items.summary: Sampling configurations in thermodynamic equilibrium is a long-standing challenge in statistical physics. Boltzmann generators address this problem by employing generative models to propose independent configurations, which are then reweighted via importance sampling using exact likelihood evaluations. Recent Boltzmann Generators based on continuous normalizing flows and flow matching have achieved significant success for particle systems and biomolecules. However, these approaches have not been extended to amorphous materials (glasses), for which equilibrium sampling is notoriously slow. Because of their disordered structure, the invariances and geometrical constraints of amorphous materials differ from those of crystals and biomolecules, preventing the direct use of existing generative models. Here, we develop Boltzmann Generators tailored to amorphous materials by building the required equivariances directly into Riemannian stochastic interpolants. Our framework incorporates periodic boundary conditions and particle symmetries using equivariant graph neural networks. Numerical experiments demonstrate that enforcing physical symmetries significantly improves the accuracy of Boltzmann Generators, but also reveal an intrinsic limitation of the continuous-flow formulation: accumulated numerical errors during likelihood integration break time-reversibility, compromising exact thermodynamic reweighting. These results reveal a fundamental challenge for continuous-flow generative models in statistical mechanics and call for alternative approaches that preserve exact thermodynamic consistency.

items.title: Effect of deuteration on methane cluster stability
items.summary: The evaporation from clusters of mixed deuterated and protonated methane molecules has been studied experimentally and theoretically. Only loss of the two components CH$_4$ and CD$_4$ is observed, showing the absence of hydrogen scrambling. The branching ratio of the two channels scales with the mole fractions of the isotopologues, corresponding to a fixed ratio of 1.5 for the CH$_4$ and CD$_4$ rates. The number is explained by the combined effect of the zero-point energies found in quantum chemical calculations and the use of detailed balance to describe the evaporation process, the latter by incorporating the moment of inertia of the two isotopologue molecules and their rotational degrees of freedom. The difference in evaporative activation energies is determined to be 6.1~\% and 6.8~\% from two experimental determinations and 8.7~\% theoretically with B3LYP+GD3BJ, corresponding to 5--7~meV. The same theory finds the CH$_4$ activation energy to be 83.8 meV, close to the experimental bulk value of 84.7 meV. Differences in Helmholtz free energies of decay products are extracted from the experimental data, yielding the molecular mixing as the only contribution to the entropy term.

items.title: Acoustic Illusion of a Rigid Object for a Moving Emitter via Equivalent Surface Control
items.summary: We report a three-dimensional acoustic illusion of a rigid object illuminated by an emitter moving along an arbitrary trajectory. The object is absent: control sources are arranged around its location, the closed surface they define being termed the equivalent surface. Driven by the field the object would have scattered onto this surface, the sources radiate, by the Kirchhoff--Helmholtz representation, that same field beyond it. The control signals follow in closed form from a time-dependent physical optics formulation that we derive for a moving emitter, in which the motion enters analytically through the acoustic travel times, so that the scattering problem need not be re-solved at each emitter position, nor the propagation domain discretized. For objects too large to enclose, the signals are mapped onto an internal surface, an option whose advantages and penalties are discussed. Numerical simulations validate the method in both configurations.

items.title: Framework for atom-resolved decomposition of second-harmonic generation in nonlinear optical crystals
items.summary: In this work, we develop a new framework for computing atom-resolved contributions to optical properties based on atoms-in-molecules (AIM) schemes. The formalism is independent of the specific AIM method and is made rigorous by partitioning momentum matrix elements into atomic contributions while exactly satisfying the relevant sum rules. Zincblende GaP provides a two-atom demonstration of the atom-resolved second-harmonic-generation (SHG) analysis using five AIM partitioning methods. The two-center Ga--P channels account for $80.6$--$82.2\%$ of the SHG response, despite the pronounced partition dependence of the atomic charges. We then apply the framework to six representative ultraviolet nonlinear-optical crystals: $β$-BaB$_2$O$_4$ (BBO), LiB$_3$O$_5$ (LBO), CsB$_3$O$_5$ (CBO), CsLiB$_6$O$_{10}$ (CLBO), KBe$_2$BO$_3$F$_2$ (KBBF), and LiCs$_2$PO$_4$ (LCPO). The atom-triplet decomposition shows that two-center channels dominate the principal SHG components, while on-site terms are smaller and multicenter terms provide an important secondary contribution. Although the AIM charges, detailed local percentages, and exact pathway ranks depend on the partition, the physical interpretation remains stable across the tested AIM methods. B/O-only pathways dominate the leading responses of KBBF and LBO. Mixed pathways involving B/O or P/O atoms and cations make substantial contributions to the leading responses of BBO, CBO, CLBO, and LCPO. The decomposition framework therefore establishes a quantitative connection between local response pathways and the bulk nonlinear-optical response.

items.title: Beyond the Beacon: State and Corporate Competition after an Information-Rich Technosignature Detection
items.summary: The 2026 update to the Declaration of Principles Concerning the Conduct of the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence provides a framework for post-detection practice. Like earlier versions, it addresses information content directly: a confirmation report should record any detected content, and the underlying data, methods, and code should be openly preserved and disseminated. The declaration is necessarily concise and is intended to be supported by supplementary material that examines specific issues in greater depth. This paper contributes to that process by considering the possible detection of an information-rich technosignature: a signal carrying data, imagery, or machine-readable content. Whereas the prevailing concept of a detection remains that of a beacon, a signal with recoverable and potentially exploitable content would shift much of the post-detection challenge from verification to information stewardship, while encouraging competitive efforts to decode and use the signal. Few studies have addressed this scenario directly, and the geopolitical literature has so far framed post-detection competition mainly in terms of state actors. Large corporations now possess the computing power, AI capabilities, and, in some cases, receiving infrastructure needed to independently pursue an extraterrestrial signal without any obligation to disclose their findings. This largely unexamined dimension materially changes the post-detection landscape. These considerations bear directly on the declaration's commitment to openness and transparency, and on how that commitment can be upheld when powerful actors outside the SETI community may not share it. I identify information-rich technosignatures as a topic for supplementary guidance and offer a preliminary set of questions for the community to consider.

items.title: Reliability-Aware Refinement of High-Resolution Human Mobility Origin-Destination Tables under Sparsity and Suppression
items.summary: High-resolution origin-destination (OD) tables derived from digital mobility traces can preserve fine-scale collective movement structure, but sampling, population expansion, and privacy-motivated low-count suppression create heterogeneous observational support across OD entries and make apparent zeros difficult to interpret. We develop a reliability-aware refinement framework that combines each released OD entry with a time-resolved, data-informed radiation baseline through a closed-form cell-wise Gamma-Poisson update, without smoothing neighboring OD pairs. Applied to a 125 m hourly Tokyo OD product, the method preserves concentrated directional flows while adding lower-intensity, baseline-supported links. The relative contribution of released and model-supported structure varies substantially across OD pairs and departure hours, including among positive-flow entries: released flows are most strongly retained at 7:00, followed by 17:00, whereas the radiation baseline contributes more at 13:00. The inferred characteristic radius broadens the movement range represented by the baseline and exhibits structured variation around major station areas and rail corridors. Tokyo and Fukuoka also show a common increase in data-baseline separation at long distances. Under controlled Poisson thinning, calibrated refinement yields lower realization-averaged mean absolute error than an independently resampled no-refinement table across the tested conditions. This experiment provides internal calibration under imposed degradation, not external validation against true unsuppressed flows. The framework thus provides a transparent way to preserve fine-scale empirical mobility structure while making the cell-wise contribution of structured model support explicit.

items.title: Electronic Properties of Ladder-Type Phenylenes Studied by Thermally-Assisted-Occupation Density Functional Theory
items.summary: Accurate prediction of the electronic properties of extended $π$-conjugated systems with radical character remains a major theoretical challenge. To overcome this challenge, thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) has been developed in recent years. In this study, we employ TAO-DFT to systematically explore the electronic properties of ladder-type phenylenes ($n$-LPs), containing $n$ linearly fused four-membered carbon rings. Our calculations reveal that all investigated $n$-LPs (with $n$ = 1 ~ 40) possess singlet ground states. With increasing $n$-LP length, we observe a transition from the nonradical character of shorter $n$-LPs to the polyradical character of longer $n$-LPs. Notably, we identify a distinct damped periodic oscillation in the radical character of $n$-LPs, featuring highly correlated hotspots at specific lengths ($n = 3k - 1$, where $k$ are positive integers). The real-space representation of active orbitals confirms this global electronic behavior is governed by the intrinsic structural periodicity and completely delocalized nature of the active orbitals along the central ladder framework. These findings provide fundamental insights into the size-dependent electronic properties of $n$-LPs, guiding their rational design for future nanomaterial applications.

items.title: Popularity-driven interactions in multilayer bounded-confidence opinion dynamics
items.summary: Social media users interact with their own social networks but also with platform-wide content, where a small number of highly popular users may receive a disproportionate share of attention. In this paper, we study how those interactions outside the social networks and user popularity regulate the formation of opinion clusters. We design a bounded-confidence opinion dynamics model on a multilayer network consisting of a social network coupled to a fully connected explore layer of potential interaction contacts. We show that uniform sampling on the explore layer increases mixing across social neighbourhoods and reduces opinion diversity while also weakening the influence of the underlying social network. We then introduce a popularity-driven interaction mechanism in which contact selection is biased by a time-evolving popularity score, so that frequently selected users become increasingly likely to be re-selected. The resulting concentration of explore-layer interactions on a small number of highly popular users reduces the homogenising effect of the explore layer, increasing opinion diversity. The resulting changes relative to a single-layer system depend on the underlying social network structure. As the popularity inequality increases, a small number of highly popular users can act as opinion attractors and sustain polarisation in regimes where the corresponding model without popularity heterogeneity converges to consensus.

items.title: Fast, parallel, three-dimensional rearrangement of atom arrays using superpositions of elementary holograms
items.summary: Assembling defect-free arrays of neutral atoms requires real-time rearrangement of stochastically loaded optical tweezers. Conventional rearrangement methods shuttle atoms sequentially, whereas high-speed spatial light modulators (SLMs) can move all atoms in parallel, which scales more favorably as the array size grows. For fast parallel rearrangement, the sequence of holograms displayed on the SLM should be computed more rapidly than the SLM refresh rate, and there should be phase continuity between successive holograms to minimize transient intensity fluctuations. We calculate holograms analytically by adding together the complex fields needed to produce each individual trap, and we ramp the phase of each trap linearly as it moves to its target location. Trap positions enter as continuous variables, rather than tied to points on a grid, so the method provides high positioning accuracy. Using a single GPU, we compute each intermediate hologram in 0.284 ms, considerably faster than the SLM refresh time of 0.696 ms, so the rearrangement speed is hardware-limited. In each step, we use the free processing time to iteratively optimize the holograms for equal intensity across the traps, decreasing trap non-uniformity to 1.24% during rearrangement at no cost in total time. Starting from an array of 256 sites loaded stochastically with $^{87}$Rb atoms, we assemble a 100-atom array in under 20 ms with a rearrangement survival probability of 99.31(12)% per atom. This rearrangement increases the temperature of the atoms by 9(3) $μ$K, which is small compared to the trap depth of 480 $μ$K. Our method can also move individual atoms axially, enabling transport in different planes. We demonstrate this capability with a rearrangement protocol where one set of atoms leapfrogs over another.

items.title: Cooperation Dynamics with Environmental Feedback: Steady States and Transitions
items.summary: Cooperative behavior and its regulatory mechanisms are central to complex systems and evolutionary game theory. In natural populations, strategy updates and endogenous payoff environments interact bidirectionally, shaping cooperation. We propose a strategy-payoff environmental-feedback model for four canonical games: Prisoner's Dilemma, Snowdrift, Stag-Hunt, and Harmony. Mathematical derivation reduces the high-dimensional coupled system to an analytically equivalent canonical replicator equation. Bifurcation diagrams, phase portraits, and simulations show how initial cooperation, temptation to defect, and punishment jointly regulate cooperation. Stag-Hunt and Harmony display bistability and initial-state dependence; Prisoner's Dilemma exhibits robust dynamics with stable mixed equilibria. Temptation and punishment drive sequential cross-type game transitions at critical thresholds. Sufficient punishment suppresses defection, shifts bifurcation thresholds, delays destabilization of cooperative steady states, and reshapes these transitions. Numerical tests confirm equivalence and stability switching. Spatial lattice simulations agree with theoretical predictions, supporting robustness. This work reveals regulatory mechanisms from endogenous payoff feedback and initial-condition sensitivity, providing a basis for understanding and optimizing collective prosocial behavior.

items.title: Effect of leading edge geometry on aerodynamic performance of a flat plate
items.summary: Flow separation around flat plate is influenced by the thickness and leading edge geometry, which creates the shear stresses and pressure distribution manifesting into unsteady aerodynamic forces. Leading edge geometries have been widely reported but the influence of leading edge curvature at low Reynolds numbers (Re) have found less attention. The present study uses two dimensional numerical simulation to investigate the effect of a hemispherical curvature (protuberance) at the leading edge and reports how vortex shedding, shedding frequencies and aerodynamic forces are affected over a range of angles of attack ($0^\circ \leq α\leq 25^\circ$) at Re = 1000. Thicker vortical regions are formed near the plate with curvature at the leading edge. Onset of shedding is noted at angle of attack of $5^\circ$ for the plate with curvature at the leading edge and it gets delayed for simple flat plate. The temporal force coefficients on the plates show multiple frequencies at higher angles of attack. The plate with curvature at the leading edge has a glide ratio of 1 at $0^\circ$ angle of attack and has equivalent glide ratio to that of simple flat plate at higher angles of attack. The simple flat plate has better glide ratios at moderate angles of attack like $5^\circ, 10^\circ$ and $15^\circ$. The results will help in making engineering informed design decisions for smaller unmanned aerial/aquatic vehicles cruising at low Reynolds numbers.

items.title: Mobility energetic balance frames spatial configuration of cities
items.summary: Urban spatial configurations emerge as the result of interactions between citizens' activities, movements and the landscape. Topography forms part of the physical settings through which mobility occurs, influencing movement energetic requirements. Using road networks, elevation data and mobility flows inferred from geolocated records, we define a simplified comparative measure of movement energy and test how it changes when the observed urban configuration is translated, rotated or rescaled within its topographic setting while mobility demand is held fixed. Across 56 cities, observed configurations consistently show lower movement energy requirements than most of the alternative configurations examined. This recurrent pattern reveals a measurable relationship between topography and urban spatial organization and is compatible with cumulative adaptation among urban structure, mobility and terrain. These findings add an energetic dimension to our understanding of how topography relates to urban spatial organization and provide an empirical basis for considering terrain-related movement requirements when evaluating future urban growth and densification.

items.title: A linear model of synergetic current drive with lower-hybrid wave and electron cyclotron wave
items.summary: A linear model of synergetic current drive (SCD) with lower-hybrid wave (LHW) and electron cyclotron wave (ECW) is developed to quickly calculate the quantitative SCD efficiency and reveal the conditions for the occurrence of the synergy effect. In this model, the response function dominated by collisions in the presence of LHW is derived from the adjoint equations by using perturbation and Green-Function techniques, where the relativistic and trapping effects are considered. The SCD results compared to Lin-Liu's ECW current drive (ECCD) efficiency show two features of the synergy effect, one is that it is inclined to occur at smaller $y = 2ω_{c}/ω$ with the fixed ECW parallel refractive index $n_{\parallel}$, and the other is that the threshold values of $y$, at which the synergy effect becomes sufficiently significant, shift towards higher values with a decreasing $n_{\parallel}$; the SCD results without the trapping effect and the response function without the relativistic effect have been provided. The quasilinear simulation on ECCD and SCD efficiency with a two-dimensional Fokker-Planck code is consistent with the results of the linear model in trends. Given considerable parameter improvements nowadays, the SCD efficiencies with parameters of current mainstream reactors are calculated in this work. We provide the current profile of ECCD and SCD by combining them with GENRAY, showing the potential application of integrating SCD into a ray-tracing code. Criteria for the occurrence and the sufficient significance of the synergy effect are suggested, which indicate that the synergy effect is dependent on the power factor that quantifies the degree of the overlap of the two waves quasilinear domains, the LHW power, and synergy electrons.

items.title: Quantitative validation of SMBI deposition profiles on EAST using experimentally constrained simulations
items.summary: Quantitative comparison between SMBI fueling simulations and experiments has long been hampered by the poor constraint on the effective source. Here, the particle increment per pulse is extracted experimentally and used to calibrate the simulation source. For EAST shot 71438, the density evolution from microwave reflectometry is analyzed for nine SMBI pulse groups. The SMBI-induced density increase is isolated from the background by comparing the rising and falling phases around each pulse group. Its radial profile peaks in the mid-pedestal region for every pulse group. Volume integration of this increment provides the experimental reference. The simulations use a multi-fluid model in the BOUT++ framework in which two transport operators are recast into conservative flux form, with the particle balance residual reduced to about 2% of the injected amount, and the perpendicular transport coefficients are constructed from the discrete radial flux balance, with the unphysical changes of the initial density and temperature profiles in source-free evolution reduced by an order of magnitude. For three cases sharing the same nominal molecular flux, the simulated deposition peak agrees with the experimental one in the relative pedestal coordinate. The simulated conversion of the injected particles at the end of the injection is slightly lower than the value inferred from the experiment, while the fraction retained at the end of the pulse is higher. The perturbation thus decays more slowly in the simulation, which we attribute to fast loss channels not represented in the model, such as parallel losses to the scrape-off layer. The edge electron temperature stays on the high-temperature plateau of the dissociation and ionization rate coefficients throughout the pulse, and the inward shift of the deposition with edge cooling reported earlier does not occur under the present conditions.

items.title: Imaging defects in two-dimensional crystals by convergent beam electron diffraction
items.summary: Convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED), recently demonstrated on two-dimensional (2D) materials, offers a number of interesting applications such as imaging atomic in- and out-of plane shifts, interlayer distances, and individual adsorbates. In this study, we show how CBED allows for atomic-precision imaging of individual defects in 2D materials using one single-shot intensity measurement. In combination with structural calculations using density functional theory, we present simulated CBED patterns for various defects in graphene, each of which exhibits a unique fingerprint distribution. We also show how atomic positions, including the individual atomic defects in graphene, can be reconstructed by iterative phase retrieval from a single CBED pattern.

items.title: LAO+: Focused, Multi-Replica Accelerated Orthogonal Sampling for Robust Binding Free Energy Predictions
items.summary: We introduce Lambda-ABF-OPES+ ($\text{LAO+}$), a multi-replica framework for absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations that accelerates both the alchemical transformation and the slow ``orthogonal'' motions coupled to it. At the core of $\text{LAO+}$ is a partitioned $λ$-dynamics scheme that concentrates sampling on the abrupt rehydration of the binding pocket, the main bottleneck of ligand decoupling, while Hamiltonian replica exchange relays configurations along the entire alchemical path. This drives a fourfold gain in convergence speed for the rate-limiting leg over our previous $\text{LAO}$ method, which was itself up to ninefold faster than Lambda-ABF, an overall gain of up to $\sim$36-fold. Applied to 28 protein--ligand complexes across five targets, $\text{LAO+}$ achieves a root-mean-square error of 0.83~kcal~mol$^{-1}$ and a correlation of 0.87 with experiment from only 63~ns of sampling per ligand. Moreover, dedicated reservoir replicas accelerate any slow degree of freedom that can be described by a collective variable. We demonstrate this by recovering hidden protein and ligand conformational states, for example in T4 lysozyme, BRD4 and JNK1. Together, these advances make accurate ABFE calculations practical for drug discovery.

items.title: Space Sustainability: The Global Commons
items.summary: Space is no longer a distant, barely reachable frontier of scientific exploration; it has become a critical infrastructure for life on Earth and a rapidly expanding zone of intense commercial activity. Yet this expansion is unfolding in ways that replicate, and amplify, the unsustainable dynamics already driving ecological and social crises on our planet. This chapter explains the concept of space sustainability as a multidimensional challenge; it raises the questions of governance, knowledge, power, justice, and global responsibility. It highlights both the profound benefits derived from space activities and the uneven distribution of costs and risks, from orbital debris and atmospheric impacts to privatization of essential services. We therefore argue that it frames space as a global commons that demands stewardship rather than pure exploitation, cooperation rather than competition, and governance that prioritizes long-term wellbeing rather than laissez-faire approach. Sustainability in space is inseparable from sustainability on Earth. This chapter invites readers, whether they are space administration and industry actors, policymakers, scientists, or simply engaged citizens, to see space not as a limitless frontier, but as a shared domain whose future depends on collective choices made today.

items.title: Multiplicative Path Weights in Networks: From Katz Connectivity to Mean First-Passage Times
items.summary: Signal dispersion, stress propagation in interbank systems, and transmission probabilities in epidemic and reliability models are all captured by studying paths on directed graphs where the path weight is defined as the product of its edge weights. Connectivity in such networks is naturally quantified by aggregating these multiplicative path weights across nodes. This paper provides a comprehensive treatise on connectivity and ranking measures based on multiplicative path weights. We demonstrate how standard all-path connectivity, such as the standard Katz centrality, can be extended beyond its classical spectral threshold. In addition, we derive closed-form expressions for connectivity based on first-hit paths and introduce a new version of Katz centrality. Furthermore, for random edge weights, we derive resolvent-based expressions for the first and second moments, alongside variance bounds, under a path-indexed coupling framework. Finite irreducible Markov chains are a subclass of the models studied, and we show that the scaled matrix of first-hit path probabilities is the probability-generating function for first-passage and return times, and that differentiation yields the classical first-passage times. Numerical examples illustrate the application of our results in a variety of settings.

items.title: Casimir forces on suspended thin dielectric membranes covered with graphene
items.summary: We investigate the Casimir force on thin suspended dielectric layers covered with graphene, both theoretically and experimentally. Thermal effects of the Casimir force on graphene occur at separations significantly smaller compared to ordinary metals and dielectrics. At such small separations, the Casimir force is sufficiently strong to be measured experimentally. However, the presence of substrates to support the graphene significantly reduces the enhancement. We show theoretically that replacing the solid substrate beneath graphene with a thin dielectric membrane partially restores this strong thermal dependence. One of the interacting objects is a solid gold plate. The other object is a suspended dielectric membrane made of either 15 nm of silicon oxide or 13 nm silicon nitride, covered with graphene. At a separation of $\sim$500 nm, theoretical predictions yield changes in the Casimir pressure of up to 54 % and 40 % for silicon oxide and silicon nitride, respectively, when the temperature is increased from 10 K to 294 K. Measurements were performed for graphene on a suspended silicon nitride membrane at room temperature, using a gold-coated sphere attached to a cantilever as the force sensor. The measured force gradient is consistent with the theoretical prediction, although the thermal dependence could not be resolved, in part because of uncertainties in the optical properties of silicon nitride. Replacing a bulk substrate with a thin dielectric membrane covered with graphene provides a substantial reduction of the Casimir force, which may facilitate the stable operation of neutral nanomechanical elements at small separations.

items.title: Machine Learning Surrogate Model for Accelerating InGaAs/GaAs Quantum Well Laser Design
items.summary: A machine-learning surrogate model based on a multi-layer perceptron neural network is used to predict six laser performance metrics for an indium gallium arsenide quantum well laser given epitaxial layer parameters as inputs. The surrogate model was trained on simulation data from a set of 4999 designs which were generated by varying epitaxial layer parameters and simulating each design with Harold to extract performance metrics. The model predicts all 6 chosen metrics with a coefficient of determination, $R^2$, greater than 0.91 on a held-out test set and demonstrates a $\sim 10^6 \times$ speed up compared to full device simulations. The model is used to search across 1 million potential epitaxial designs in the parameter space and find designs that minimize threshold current and internal loss. Using the surrogate, rather than full device simulation, reduces computation time for a million designs from 231 days to $\sim$2 minutes on a standard laptop. It is also demonstrated that use of the Swish activation function, rather than ReLU, together with engineered input features - i.e. derived quantities calculated from the base model inputs - raise the mean $R^2$ from 0.88 to 0.94 without additional training data, and reduce the mean absolute percentage error from $1.78 \pm 0.08 \%$ to $1.17 \pm 0.09 \%$.

items.title: Bayesian Joint Reconstruction and Uncertainty Quantification for Limited-Data Multi-Contrast X-Ray CT
items.summary: Multi-contrast X-ray computed tomography (CT) combines attenuation contrast with phase and dark-field contrast, which are sensitive to refraction and ultra-small-angle scattering, respectively. Common implementations record several intensity measurements per projection angle by phase or mask stepping, which lengthens acquisition and, at a fixed exposure per measurement, raises the dose. Limited-data acquisition via sparse angular sampling or reduced stepping lowers these costs but makes the data less informative, calling for prior information and uncertainty quantification. We study joint Bayesian reconstruction of attenuation, phase, and dark-field images from separately retrieved sinograms. A joint total variation term in the prior couples edge locations across the images but not their values. Posterior sampling with the No-U-Turn Sampler complements maximum a posteriori estimates with pixel-wise uncertainty. We compare this joint prior with channel-wise total variation alone on synthetic and experimental Talbot-Lau interferometry data under full, sparse-angle, sparse-step, and combined acquisition (up to 24 times fewer exposures). Both maximum a posteriori reconstructions suppressed undersampling artifacts, with synthetic relative errors 1.6-11 times lower than those of filtered backprojection. The joint prior gave modest synthetic accuracy gains, a cleaner experimental dark-field background, 23-30 % lower mean dark-field posterior standard deviation, and 4-38% higher median effective sample size in experimental limited-data runs. In the synthetic study, posterior standard deviations matched or exceeded the errors in flat regions but underestimated them at boundaries, especially in phase. Experimental phase chains mixed slowly under angular undersampling. The formulation also applies to edge illumination with adapted forward and noise models.

items.title: Nonreciprocal Control of Spatiotemporal Floquet Dynamics in Levitated Optomechanical Arrays
items.summary: Periodically driven photonic and optomechanical systems provide a versatile setting for realizing collective Floquet dynamics, yet the relation between temporal locking and continuous rotation of the finite-$q$ pattern remains poorly understood. We show that a nonreciprocal ring of parametrically driven optically levitated particles allows the spatial phase to be controlled while collective temporal locking is preserved. Nonreciprocity polarizes the counterpropagating finite-wave-vector modes and drives a transition from the pinned state to persistent directional spatial-phase drift. The normalized spatial-phase drift velocity is independently encoded in the splitting of the two dominant spectral branches, and its direction reverses with the coupling asymmetry. The pinned regime exhibits a laboratory frame period-two time-crystalline response, whereas the rotating regime forms a distinct temporally locked spatiotemporally ordered state. The same correspondence between spatial-phase drift and spectral splitting persists down to few-particle rings, indicating that the effect does not require a large array. These results establish nonreciprocity as a route to independently control spatial-phase drift and temporal synchronization in driven levitated optomechanical systems.

items.title: Algebraic coefficients of fractional parentage for three particles in the oscillator Jacobi basis
items.summary: We present a closed-form construction of the orbital coefficients of fractional parentage (CFP) of three identical particles in the translationally invariant harmonic oscillator (HO) Jacobi basis. These are usually obtained by numerically diagonalizing a permutation operator in every energy-angular-momentum block. We show this diagonalization is unnecessary. Dressing the class operator $P_{13} + P_{23}$ with the single unitary $W = H^1 Φ$ -- a fixed complexification followed by the HO bracket with mass parameter $d=1$ -- turns it into the label swap times an integer. Every CFP is then the single ket $|K_{i,s}\rangle = 2Q^s W^\dagger|i\rangle$ -- a 2-scaled, sign-decorated column of the $d=1$ bracket restricted to one $e_2$-parity of the labels -- whose norm, $1 + s\langle i | J | i \rangle$, is itself a single matrix element. The same $W$ carries label parity into swap symmetry, $W Q^s W^\dagger = R^s$, making the bookkeeping collapse. The eigenvalues are exact integers $\pm 2$ and $\pm 1$ labeling the $S(3)$ symmetry classes. The construction is uniform in $E$, $L$ and symmetry class, reducing CFP-specific work from $O(n^3)$ to $O(n^2)$ in block dimension. An eigensolver remains only inside the bracket engine supplying $H^1$, where all residual numerical error originates. We implement this on an SU(3)-basis bracket engine, checking all 1301 blocks up to $E=50$ (912 366 CFPs, largest block $2907 \times 2907$): the $S(3)$ class assignment is exact everywhere. The residual numerical error (entirely the bracket engine's) stays below $10^{-8}$ for $E \leq 35$, restoring to $\leq 10^{-22}$ via a quadruple-precision build beyond that. We further validate against independently generated antisymmetrization data of a production three-nucleon code, including the $^3$He ground-state energy.

items.title: Monte Carlo Framework for Physics-Based Design and Optimization of X-Ray Compressive Ghost Imaging Systems
items.summary: X-ray ghost imaging has emerged as a promising computational imaging modality capable of forming images from spatially integrated measurements. Unlike optical implementations, image formation is governed by multiple energy-dependent photon-matter interactions: photoelectric absorption, Compton scattering, and fluorescence. The relative contributions of these interactions depend on the source spectrum, sample geometry and composition, and detector configuration. We present a FLUKA-based Monte Carlo framework that models photon transport and predicts bucket signals generated by binary illumination patterns. The framework couples a physical scaling analysis, which converts the simulated bucket signals into photon numbers, tube loading and absorbed dose, with a ghost imaging reconstruction analysis of image quality and convergence. Our framework helps assess whether a given configuration is limited by the source output, the mask modulation or the reconstruction before any measurement is made. We evaluate the reconstruction for a centimeter-scale imaging system for an iron crown using one transmission detector and three off-axis scattering detectors over a range of source spectra. The results reveal how source characteristics and detector geometry influence reconstruction quality and radiation dose, providing quantitative guidelines for future X-ray ghost imaging system design. More broadly, this work establishes a predictive design framework for application-specific X-ray ghost imaging systems.

items.title: RAT-EC: Introducing a New Open-Source 3D Volume-Integral Eddy-Current Module
items.summary: We present RAT-EC, an open-source volume-integral eddy-current module for unstructured meshes, driven in the time domain by coils of arbitrary winding geometry. It is the first openly available code of this kind and part of the open-source RAT suite. Because only the conductor is meshed, neither the surrounding air nor an artificial outer boundary has to be modelled, which simplifies model preparation and brings problems with thin gaps and intricate air regions within reach of standard hardware. The formulation combines a semi-analytical evaluation of the singular and near-singular inductance terms, a multi-level fast multipole method that accelerates both the far-field inductance action and the coil field, topology-aware constraints for multiply connected conductors, and a matrix-free, GPU-accelerated time integration. The implementation is verified against closed-form solutions for a conducting sphere and a conducting ring, and is validated on the TEAM-7 benchmark. At 50 Hz, RAT-EC reproduces the measured field as accurately as finite-element solutions. At 200 Hz, it agrees with a converged finite-element model, but both deviate from published measurements, which suggests that this benchmark point should be re-examined. RAT-EC provides an open platform for volume-integral eddy-current simulation and method development.

items.title: On the fairness of single round-robin tournaments: Evidence from European football
items.summary: Single round-robin tournaments are widely regarded as unfair because of their home-away imbalance: some competitors play more home games than the others. Therefore, most sports leagues are played in a double round-robin format. However, some European football leagues contain a single round-robin (sub)tournament. To test whether empirical data can validate their unfairness, we construct a unique database and develop a strength of schedule metric based on Elo ratings with favourable theoretical properties. In contrast to the robust impact of relative team strength, the strength of schedule is found to have no significant effect on the number of points scored under the assumption of a league-specific home advantage. Consequently, the theoretical unfairness is not a serious issue in practice, or the standard approach of modelling home advantage in Elo ratings might need to be reconsidered.

items.title: When is vaccine prioritization worth optimizing?
items.summary: Optimizing vaccine prioritization is often treated as the default policy response when vaccine supply is limited. Yet optimized prioritization carries administrative, ethical and communication costs, motivating an upstream question: whether differences among vaccine allocations can alter epidemic outcomes enough to make optimization epidemiologically necessary. We show that optimization is not always worth pursuing: in some regimes, vaccination markedly reduces epidemic burden, but many feasible allocation rules perform almost equally well, making the necessity of optimization low. We quantify this necessity as the range of epidemic outcomes generated by different allocations under fixed supply and show that it is governed by competition between vaccinating high-contact groups to slow transmission and vaccinating groups that benefit most directly: necessity is low when these protection routes are balanced and high when one dominates. Increasing transmission intensity changes this balance and drives a transition in the optimal allocation from transmission-focused prioritization toward direct protection. Different prevention objectives exhibit distinct transition thresholds, creating regimes in which optimizing one objective substantially compromises another, thereby revealing when the choice of prevention target matters most. This framework reframes vaccine prioritization as a prior decision problem, identifying when optimization is warranted, when simpler rules suffice, and when prevention goals conflict.

items.title: Energy Flow Shapes the Decomposition Dynamics of a Reactive Atmospheric Intermediate
items.summary: The unimolecular dynamics of Criegee intermediates depend strongly on their internal energy, which can differ substantially between nascent atmospheric species and laboratory-prepared reactants. Here, the decomposition dynamics of {\it anti-}CH$_3$CHOO are investigated using molecular dynamics simulations on a neural network-based potential energy surface under thermal and mode-selective vibrational excitation. Simulations were performed at internal energies representative of those released during ozonolysis (chemical/thermal preparation, TP) or following vibrational excitation (VibEx) along the CH-stretching mode with two or three quanta, as can be done in laboratory studies. These excitation conditions strongly affect reaction yields and kinetics, with VibEx promoting passage across the initial cyclization barrier. For TP, 35 kcal/mol of internal energy are required to form molecular products, whereas for VibEx, 27 kcal/mol are sufficient. Although TP and VibEx ensembles access largely the same fragmentation pathways with comparable relative yields, the absolute product yields, characteristic timescales, and kinetic behavior differ substantially. Methyldioxirane is found to be a kinetic trap along the pathway. The resulting molecular-level description of {\it anti-}CH$_3$CHOO decomposition provides guidance for interpreting experiments and contributes to a broader understanding of energy-dependent Criegee-intermediate dynamics.

items.title: Chiroptical Nonlinearity Found in Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.summary: Chiroptical nonlinearity is vital for modern optics and photonics. However, it remains a central challenge to obtain a material simultaneously with large second-order nonlinearity and strong nonlinear optical chirality. Here we uncover the strong chiroptical nonlinearity in COF-330-a, owing to the formation of unique chiral, polar structure with large p-electron conjugation via structural transformation. A large effective second-order nonlinear susceptibility of ~ 101 pm/V and a strong nonlinear chiroptical response (SHG-CD: -1.60 to +1.66) have been demonstrated in individual COF-330-a microcrystals, transcending the performance trade-off limitation in conventional chiroptical materials. These findings open a new avenue for designing nonlinear chiroptical materials which harness the duality of polarity and chirality and chemical versatility of COFs.

items.title: Linear causality and stability constraints on relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics
items.summary: In this work, we construct a theoretical framework for relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics based on entropy current analysis. The formalism consistently incorporates finite relaxation dynamics of the dissipative fluxes, providing a transient framework suitable for analyzing linear stability and short-wavelength causality. Utilizing linear mode analysis, we investigate the constraints imposed by causality and stability on this anisotropic system. By linearizing the theory around a homogeneous equilibrium state, we identify the magnetosonic, Alfvén, and charge-diffusion sectors, together with their coupling terms. For each sector, we derive asymptotic dispersion relations in both the long-wavelength (small-$k$) and short-wavelength (large-$k$) regimes, validating them against exact numerical roots. Our numerical analysis confirms the accuracy of these asymptotic solutions and uncovers a nontrivial angular dependence, especially near special propagation directions where the ordinary momentum expansion becomes less reliable. By evaluating the large-$k$ behavior of the propagating branches alongside the damping properties of non-hydrodynamic modes, we delineate the corresponding causality constraints. We find that the admissible linear causal domain is governed by the interplay between propagation direction, anisotropic transport coefficients, and relaxation times, with the resulting bounds being intrinsically mode-dependent. These findings provide a systematic theoretical basis for investigating linear stability and short-wavelength causality in relativistic magnetohydrodynamics beyond the first-order approximation.

items.title: A Panoramic Network Overview of Shortcut Impact on Power Grids
items.summary: Synchronization of coupled oscillators on complex networks underlies critical functions in natural and engineered systems, including power-grid operation. While synchronization stability on fixed network topologies has been studied extensively, less is known about how an added transmission link affects stability depending on where it is placed relative to generation and consumption. We address this question using simplified ring-network power-grid models in which producer and consumer nodes are spatially organized into clusters. Long-range transmission links, which we refer to as shortcuts, are added between non-adjacent nodes, and synchronization stability is quantified by basin stability in second-order coupled-oscillator dynamics. We compare shortcut placements across four scenarios varying network size, power allocation, power-injection heterogeneity, and producer--consumer arrangement. When producers and consumers form two spatially separated clusters, center-to-center shortcuts do not reduce the mean basin stability in the configurations examined and increase it by up to 75\% relative to the shortcut-less baseline. Peripheral shortcuts instead reduce mean basin stability by up to 28\% in some configurations despite the added connection, producing Braess-like degradation. In alternating multi-block networks, however, no single shortcut placement provides the same substantial enhancement, indicating that the center-to-center advantage does not directly generalize to more complex spatial arrangements. Representative time-domain simulations further show faster decay of frequency deviations for center-to-center than for peripheral shortcuts. These results demonstrate that the effect of added connectivity depends critically on where the new link is placed relative to the spatial organization of generation and consumption.

items.title: Molecule-by-molecule nanoresolved picosecond Purcell-enhanced emission at room-temperature in hollow plasmonic nanocone metamaterials
items.summary: Nanoscale variations in the electromagnetic environment strongly influence quantum emission processes, yet direct quantitative visualization of these effects at the single-emitter level remains challenging. By combining single-molecule super-resolution microscopy with time-correlated single-photon counting (TCSPC), we read the local electromagnetic environment of each molecule from its position and its excited-state lifetime. Using wafer-scale arrays of hollow plasmonic nanocones, we map position-dependent variations in the local density of optical states (LDOS) along the nanocone axis. We observe pronounced LDOS gradients that evidence a shortening of the fluorescence lifetime from nanoseconds to few picoseconds. The measured decay rates along the nanocone axis with maximum value at the top ring, yielding a total spontaneous-emission rate enhancement of more than two orders of magnitude at the single-molecule level, reaching an enhancement of the total spontaneous-emission rate of up to two orders of magnitude at the single-molecule level, in agreement with numerical simulations. These results provide direct experimental access to three-dimensional electromagnetic landscapes and establish a non-perturbative platform for quantitative molecular nanosensing in complex photonic architectures. The approach opens new opportunities for engineered room-temperature photon sources, vectorial field sensing, and scalable integrated nanophotonic technologies.

items.title: Constrained Nuclear-Electronic Orbital Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory for Excited-State Dynamics with Nuclear Quantum Effects
items.summary: Nuclear quantum effects can strongly influence excited-state processes involving light nuclei, yet their inclusion in practical molecular dynamics remains challenging. We develop constrained nuclear-electronic orbital time-dependent density functional theory (CNEO-TDDFT), which incorporates quantum-nuclear delocalization into full-dimensional effective excited-state potential energy surfaces while retaining the formal structure and computational scaling of conventional TDDFT. Analytic gradients are also developed, enabling efficient on-the-fly excited-state dynamics. CNEO-TDDFT substantially improves excited-state vibrational frequencies involving hydrogen motion and reduces the root-mean-square deviation from experiment from 113 cm$^{-1}$ to 26 cm$^{-1}$. For excited-state proton transfer in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline (HBQ), CNEO-TDDFT yields a characteristic transfer time of 14.0 fs, compared with 25.5 fs from conventional TDDFT, consistent with the experimentally inferred ultrafast timescale of 12$\pm$6 fs. These results establish CNEO-TDDFT as an accurate and efficient framework for excited-state dynamics with nuclear quantum effects.

items.title: Displacement-noise-free gravitational-wave detector using quantum tomography of photon orbital angular momentum states
items.summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) induce quantum transitions between photon orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) states with amplitudes $α_{\pm}$. Exploiting this effect, we present a displacement-noise-free detection framework that extracts GW information from the OAM Hilbert space. Parametrized quantum state tomography of the GW-induced OAM sidebands enables a single V-shaped detector to resolve all seven wave parameters: the frequency, propagation direction, two polarization amplitudes, and initial phase of each polarization. Direct detection of the sidebands yields a weak signal of approximately $10^{-15}\,\mathrm{W}$. We therefore introduce a stronger reference state $r |0>_{\mathrm{P}}$, with $r=0.01$, to enhance the detected signal. For an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $γ=0.1$, an incident light power of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, a wavelength of $λ_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$, and GW amplitudes of $A=10^{-18}$, we estimate sideband transition amplitudes of $|α_{\pm}|\sim10^{-10}$ and signal powers of order $1\,\mathrm{nW}$, scaling as $P_{\mathrm{BS}}α_{\pm}\propto P_{\mathrm{BS}}ANLγ/λ_{\mathrm{opt}}$. The shot-noise-limited sensitivity floor is $S^{1/2}_n=1.6\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$. Because the scheme measures OAM transition amplitudes rather than differential arm lengths, it is intrinsically free from displacement noise and provides a broadband probe of GWs, specifically bridging the $0.1$--$10\,\mathrm{Hz}$ mid-frequency gap.

items.title: Aluminum wide-range EOS sensitivity in Z-pinch dynamic-hohlraum liner-foam impact and outgoing radiation
items.summary: In a Z-pinch dynamic hohlraum, an aluminum liner collides with a central foam and converts kinetic energy into radiation, and the liner-foam response depends on the aluminum equation of state (EOS). We construct a wide-range aluminum equation-of-state table from density functional theory (DFT) simulations over solid-liquid-plasma regions, denoted DFT-eos. Mixed deterministic-stochastic finite-temperature DFT (mDFT) gives the electron thermal contribution; quantum molecular dynamics (QMD) with classical calibration gives the ion part. We perform one-dimensional cylindrical radiation magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) simulations at a peak current of 50 MA and rise times of 220-300 ns on a single-layer light foam load. Opacity and electrical conductivity are fixed; only the liner Al EOS is changed between DFT-eos and the quotidian EOS (QEOS). Impact time and peak liner kinetic energy change little between the two tables. Larger differences appear in flight-segment density, the contact state at impact, and the time history of outgoing radiation power at the outer interface.

items.title: AlgoPlasma: Open Algorithms for Plasma Modeling
items.summary: AlgoPlasma is an open-source library in which core numerical algorithms for plasma modeling are implemented as modular, well-documented, and independently testable components. Rather than offering a complete simulation code, it allows researchers to select, adapt, and assemble the required components into application-specific workflows. The current release is centered on particle-based simulation, while AlgoPlasma is designed to encompass a broader range of approaches to plasma modeling. It provides components for particle initialization and advancement, particle-grid coupling, field solution, collision modeling, neutral transport, selected continuity updates, probe signal analysis, and input/output, together with Message Passing Interface (MPI) exchange routines and selected Open Multi-Processing (OpenMP) kernels. Documentation links mathematical formulations to source implementations, interfaces, and usage, while verification and validation cases evaluate numerical accuracy and physical behavior. AlgoPlasma thus establishes a shared algorithmic foundation for plasma modeling, transforming repeatedly reimplemented numerical methods into open, reusable, tested, and explainable components for research, verification, education, and collaborative development.

items.title: Integrated Open-Source Framework for Simulation of Transcatheter Pulmonary Valves in Native Right Ventricular Outflow Tracts
items.summary: Pulmonary insufficiency is a consequence of transannular patch repair in Tetralogy of Fallot (ToF), leading to late morbidity and mortality. Transcatheter native outflow tract pulmonary valve replacement (TPVR) has become common, but assessment of patient candidacy and selection of the optimal device remains challenging. We demonstrate an integrated open-source workflow for simulation of TPVR in image-derived models to inform device selection. Machine learning-based segmentation of Computer Tomography (CT) scans was implemented to define the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT). A custom workflow for device positioning and pre-compression was implemented in SlicerHeart. Resulting geometries were exported to FEBio for simulation. Visualization of results and quantification were performed using custom metrics implemented in SlicerHeart and FEBio. RVOT model creation and device placement could be completed in under 1 minute. Virtual device placement using FE simulations visually mimicked actual device placement and allowed quantification of vessel strain, stress, and contact area. Regions of higher strain and stress were observed at the proximal and distal end locations of the TPVs where the devices impinge on the RVOT wall. No other consistent trends were observed across simulations. The observed variability in mechanical metrics across RVOTS, stents, and locations in the RVOT highlights that no single device performs optimally in all anatomies, thereby reinforcing the need for simulation-based patient-specific assessment. This study demonstrates the feasibility of a novel open-source workflow for the rapid simulation of TPVR, which, with further refinement, may inform assessment of patient candidacy and optimal device selection.

items.title: Simulation of topological superconductors and their competing orders using photon-mediated interactions
items.summary: Realizing and controlling the unconventional pairing featured by topological superconductors remains a central challenge. We introduce a cavity QED quantum simulator that engineers competing chiral $p_x+ip_y$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}+id_{xy}$ orders by tailoring cavity-mediated couplings between atomic pseudospins that emulate momentum-dependent pairing channels. The desired spatially inhomogeneous cavity-mediated couplings can be engineered in a 2D optical lattice using incommensurate cavity-lattice wavelengths naturally occurring in cavity QED systems. This minimal and fully tunable platform enables controlled state preparation and continuous measurement of superconducting order parameters. To probe this competition, the platform enables selective excitation and direct time-domain detection of Bardasis-Schrieffer modes---collective excitations of the subdominant pairing channel. The same competing channel can have an even stronger impact out of equilibrium, where a sudden quench can drive its growth and abruptly reshape the dominant superconducting order, despite the stability of the dominant order in equilibrium. Together, these results establish cavity QED as a controlled setting for revealing hidden competing orders and exploring nonlinear dynamics of topological superconductivity that remain elusive in solid-state and ultracold-atom systems.

items.title: Data-Driven Optimization of Seminumerical Exchange for SIMD CPUs
items.summary: We present a seminumerical exchange algorithm (SNK) based on the sn-LinK method [Laqua et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 16, 1456 (2020)], optimized for modern multi-core central processing units with single instruction multiple data vector instructions and report its implementation into the Q-Chem quantum chemistry program. Vectorization and memory management strategies for the Boys function and 3-center-1-electron (3c1e) integral kernels are given. Several new considerations are made in the computation of the 3c1e integrals: the Head-Gordon Pople horizontal recurrence relations, same-center optimizations, and multishell optimizations, all implemented symbolically employing the SymPy symbolic algebra library and exported as optimized C++ code leveraging common-sub-expression elimination (CSE) optimization techniques. A general scheme for choosing optimal integral kernels is developed through rigorous timing benchmarks. The resulting implementation is tested against traditional 4c2e exchange for several systems and basis sets, showing 1-2 orders of magnitude speedups for systems of practically relevant sizes (100-500 atoms, 2000-10000 basis functions).
