items.summary: We establish local nonpersistence of full-dimensional invariant tori with polynomially decaying actions for the periodic quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation \[ iu_t-u_{xx}+T_vu+μ|u|^4u=0,\qquad x\in\mathbb T:=\mathbb R/(2π\mathbb Z). \] For every $κ\geq1$, we construct a fixed bounded real Fourier multiplier $T_ve^{ijx}=v_je^{ijx}$ whose frequencies $λ_j=j^2+v_j$ satisfy the Bourgain-type Diophantine condition \[ \operatorname{dist}\left(\sum_j\ell_jλ_j,\mathbb Z\right) \geqγ_κ\prod_j(1+\ell_j^2\langle j\rangle^{2κ})^{-1} \] for some $γ_κ>0$ and every nonzero finitely supported integer sequence $\ell$, where $\langle j\rangle=\max\{1,|j|\}$. For this multiplier, every $3<M<4κ+\frac12$, every $A>0$, and all sufficiently small $μA^2>0$, the closed relative action tube of radius $3/10$ around $I_j=A\langle j\rangle^{-M}$ contains no full-dimensional invariant torus in $H^1(\mathbb T)$ carrying a complete flow, with arbitrary frequencies allowed. This advances the study of the polynomial-decay problem identified by Kuksin as a main open problem in KAM theory for one-dimensional Hamiltonian PDEs [Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. Ser. 2, 212 (2004), 237--258, Problem 7.1]. Bourgain discussed a related question for short-range Hamiltonian systems [Russian Math. Surveys 59 (2004), 231--246, Section 3]. The proof combines simultaneous Diophantine and weighted homological estimates, an exact common-phase transformation, and one normal-form step on four adjacent Fourier coordinates. Uniform phase rotation forces an action excursion, while overlapping parameter intervals cover all sufficiently small positive perturbations. The mechanism suggests applications to other Hamiltonian PDEs.

items.title: Edit distance exponents for irrational rotations
items.summary: We study quantitative edit-distance asymptotics for symbolic codings of irrational rotations $x \mapsto x+α$ on $\mathbb{T}$ in terms of the irrationality exponent $μ(α)$. For the binary coding determined by an interval $[0,β)$, let $d_N(x,y)$ be the edit distance between the codings of the orbits of the points $x$ and $y$ up to time $N-1$. For every $α\notin \mathbb{Q}$, almost every $β\in (0,1)$, and almost every $x,y \in \mathbb{T}$, we determine the edit-distance exponents $\displaystyle (*) \; \; \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log d_N(x,y)}{\log N} = \frac{ρ(α)}{ρ(α)+1} \; \;$ and $\; \; \displaystyle\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log d_N(x,y)}{\log N} = \min\Bigl\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{ρ(α)}\Bigr\}$, where $ ρ(α):=μ(α) - 1$. We find a surprising transition at the golden mean $\varphi= \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$: If $ ρ(α) \le \varphi$, then both asymptotics in $(*)$ hold for all $β$. However, for every finite $ρ>\varphi$, there is an uncountable set of $α$ with $ρ(α)=ρ$ for which both edit-distance exponents are strictly smaller than the corresponding values in $(*)$ for uncountably many $β$. We also derive consequences for aperiodic circle homeomorphisms and Sturmian sequences. For rotations of $\mathbb{T}^d$ coded by boxes, we prove that for almost every rotation vector, the common edit-distance exponent is $d/(d+1)$.

items.title: Polygraphic resolutions for operated algebras
items.summary: This paper introduces the structure of operated polygraphs as a categorical model for rewriting in operated algebras, generalizing Gröbner--Shirshov bases with non-monomial termination orders. We show how to construct polygraphic resolutions of free operated algebras from confluent and terminating presentations. We provide a combinatorial description of critical branchings of operated polygraphs using the structure of polyautomata introduced in this paper. Polyautomata are linear polygraphs equipped with an operator structure formalized by a pushdown automaton. Finally, we apply our constructions to several families of operated algebras, including Rota--Baxter algebras, differential algebras, and differential Rota--Baxter algebras.

items.title: Seifert cobordisms and the Chen-Yang volume conjecture
items.summary: We study the large $r$ asymptotic behavior of the Turaev-Viro invariants $TV_r(M; e^{\frac{2πi}{r}})$ of 3-manifolds with toroidal boundary, under the operation of gluing a Seifert-fibered 3-manifold along a component of $\partial M$. We show that the Turaev-Viro invariants volume conjecture is closed under this operation. As an application we prove the volume conjecture for all Seifert fibered 3-manifolds with boundary and for large classes of graph 3-manifolds.

items.title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
items.summary: Past work with Tom Seidman analyzed the spatial convergence order of the numerical finite element method applied to time-dependent diffusion-reaction equations with a measure-valued source term. For smooth source terms, the numerical method has second-order accuracy, but the non-smooth source terms introduce a limitation of the order that depends on the spatial dimension. This work in honor of Tom extends the analysis to the finite volume method in its clas- sical two-point flux form and shows that the regularity of the source term reduces the convergence order to 1 in two and 0.5 in three spatial dimensions which is reduced from the nominal second-order and depends on the space dimension. Computational tests with a point source modeled by a Dirac delta distribution exhibit the behavior predicted by the analytical results.

items.title: Poincaré's Inequality on Sliding-Window Occupation Count Kernels and the Optimal Normalized Spectral-Gap Constant
items.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible reversible Markov kernel on an $m$-state space $Ω$, and denote its right spectral gap by $\Gap(P) =1-λ_2(P)$. From a stationary trajectory, let $K_t$ be the occupation-count vector of the length-$n$ window beginning at time $t$. The stationary pair $(K_0,K_1)$ defines a reversible projected count kernel $\widetilde P_n$. For each fixed $m\ge2$, define \[ c_m^\star= \inf_{\substack{|Ω|=m,\ P\ \mathrm{irreducible\ and\ reversible} n\ge2}} \frac{n\Gap(\widetilde P_n)}{\Gap(P)}. \] We prove \[ \frac1{1080m}\le c_m^\star\le q_{m-2}, \qquad q_0=\frac14,\quad q_{r+1}=q_r(1-q_r). \] We also show $q_{m-2}=(m+\log m+O(1))^{-1}$, which implies that $c_m^\star=Θ(m^{-1})$. Thus, the reciprocal optimal comparison cost $C_m^{\mathrm{opt}}=(c_m^\star)^{-1}$ has order $m$. In the two-state case, we determine the exact values $c_2^\star=1/4$ and $C_2^{\mathrm{opt}}=4$. %the exact constants for $m\ge3$ remain open. The lower bound also holds for $n=1$ and is uniform in $P$, including sparse and periodic kernels. The proof combines short-window decorrelation with an averaged anchor-excursion decomposition, a Green-kernel hitting estimate, and a stopped Carleson--Hardy inequality. A nested rare-state construction produces finite $m$-state witnesses whose normalized Rayleigh quotients approach $q_{m-2}$ through an ordered sequence of limits. For every fixed finite irreducible reversible aperiodic kernel on at least two states, $\Gap(\widetilde P_n)=Θ_P(n^{-1})$.

items.title: Distributionally Robust Regularization of Sparse Integer Programming Trained Learning Models
items.summary: Building explainable machine learning models is crucial for human users to be able to interpret the proposed statistical relationship obtained from the training data. Mixed-integer optimization formulations are often used to train such models with explicit sparsity constraints, aiming to strike the right trade-off between sparsity and prediction accuracy. Existing methods to find the right choice of sparsity -- e.g., via cross-validation -- are computationally expensive. For convex model training formulations, recent advances in distributionally robust optimization (DRO) provide strong generalization while sidestepping this computational burden. We describe an extension of such regularization via DRO to mixed-integer sparse programs, providing statistical guarantees as a function of an associated sparsity parameter of the formulation. We illustrate the use of this approach in the case of building explainable binary classification models using sets of feature value rules.

items.title: Perfectoid Pure and Signature Pairs
items.summary: We extend perfectoid purity and related invariants to divisor pairs in mixed characteristic. The resulting purity condition agrees with $F$-purity of pairs in characteristic $p$ as defined by Hara--Watanabe. For normal (respectively, demi-normal) log $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein pairs, we show that perfectoid pure implies log canonical (respectively, semi-log canonical). We similarly establish adjunction for perfectoid pure pairs and inversion of adjunction for principal pairs in complete intersections along a Cartier divisor. We also define perfectoid pure thresholds and prove localization and base change results, including a formula for local extensions with regular closed fiber. We establish upper bounds in terms of analytic spread, dimension, and log canonical thresholds. Finally, we also introduce perfectoid signatures for divisor pairs in mixed characteristic whose positivity characterizes the BCM-regularity of log $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein pairs. We prove a transformation rule under finite extensions and show continuity and convexity for scalings of a Cartier divisor.

items.title: Multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures of generalized Johnson association schemes
items.summary: Let $\mathfrak X$ be a commutative association scheme of class $d$ on $X$. We construct the generalized Johnson association scheme $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ on partial maps from $[n]$ to $X$ with domains of size $h$. For $1\le h\le n-1$, we prove that $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ has $(d+1)$-variate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. In particular, its multivariate $Q$-polynomial property answers affirmatively a problem posed for generalized Johnson association schemes arising from finite Gelfand pairs. We also determine the primitive idempotents and the two eigenmatrices, expressing the first eigenmatrix as a product of an Eberlein polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial, and the second eigenmatrix as a product of a Hahn polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial. For the multivariate factors, we use Mizukawa--Tanaka $(d+1,2d+2)$-hypergeometric functions. In an appendix, we identify the normalized columns of the second eigenmatrix with the known spherical functions in the finite Gelfand pair case. We also discuss the orthogonality relations and the imprimitivity arising from partial maps with the same domain, and explicitly describe the multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures inherited by the blocks and the quotient.

items.title: Minimizing the makespan in job shop scheduling under conflict graph constraints
items.summary: We study the job shop scheduling problem with a conflict graph, in which adjacent jobs cannot be processed simultaneously on different machines, with the objective of minimizing the makespan. We establish a polynomial equivalence with a resource-constrained job shop problem having unit-capacity resources and binary resource requirements The problem is strongly NP-hard even on two machines with unit-time operations. For this setting, we derive an optimal-makespan formula and a linear-time algorithm when the conflict graph is a cluster graph, given the clique partition. We also develop a polynomial-time $4/3$-approximation algorithm for arbitrary conflict graphs on two machines when each job has exactly two unit-time operations. For the general problem, we propose four mixed-integer linear formulations, lower bounds, and a genetic algorithm with active, non-delay, and hybrid decoding procedures. Computational experiments on instances derived from the Lawrence and Taillard benchmarks and on randomly generated generalized job shop instances evaluate the proposed methods and show that the genetic algorithm generally improves on constructive heuristics.

items.title: Nonassociative algebras of anti-biderivation-type
items.summary: The main purpose of this paper is to study the class of Jacobi-Jordan-admissible algebras whose product is an anti-biderivation of the related Jacobi-Jordan algebra; we call them $\mathcal A{\rm BD}$-algebras. We give characterizations of $\mathcal A{\rm BD}$-algebras and show that this class includes Jacobi-Jordan algebras, symmetric anti-Leibniz algebras and anti-${\rm LR}$-algebras. The derived algebra of an anti-${\rm LR}$-algebra is associative and commutative, and all identities of its commutator algebra follow from the metabelian identity and one identity of degree $4$. We also study $\mathcal A$flexible ${\mathcal A}{\rm BD}$-algebras and prove that a complex finite-dimensional Jacobi-Jordan algebra admits a non-trivial post-Jacobi-Jordan structure if and only if its dimension is at least $3$. Finally, we give the algebraic classification of complex $3$-dimensional $\mathcal A{\rm BD}$-algebras and show that complex finite-dimensional simple ${\mathcal A}{\rm BD}$-algebras are anticommutative, while perfect ones need not be; the minimal dimension of perfect non-anticommutative ${\mathcal A}{\rm BD}$-algebras is $4$.

items.title: Saturated directed spaces and generalized clocks
items.summary: We construct a Hausdorff saturated directed space whose directed path space between two distinct points has nontrivial fundamental group although the corresponding trace space is a square. A clock is a directed space with submetrizable underlying space; a timed space is a saturated directed space equipped with a regular directed map to a clock. Over every fixed clock, timed spaces form a locally presentable category, and their quotients from paths to traces are trivial Hurewicz fibrations with continuous sections. For Hausdorff saturated directed spaces whose compact subspaces are metrizable, these quotients are trivial q-fibrations. We construct a globular clock containing the directed circle and admitting regular maps from all q-cofibrant globular realizations, whereas a finite cellular example admits no regular map to the circle. Normalization also gives a proof of the quotient theorem for execution paths and establishes the homotopy lifting property for nondecreasing reparametrizations.

items.title: Ideals in Enveloping Algebras of Loop Algebras
items.summary: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra, and consider the loop algebra $L\mathfrak g = \mathfrak g[s, s^{-1}]$ and the affine Lie algebra $\widehat{\mathfrak g}$, which is an extension of $L\mathfrak g$ by a central element $c$. It is known that the rings $\operatorname{U}(\widehat{\mathfrak g})/(c-λ)$ are simple for any nonzero scalar $λ$. On the other hand, the universal enveloping algebra $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g) \cong \mathrm{U}(\widehat{\mathfrak g})/(c)$ has many two-sided ideals, and in this paper we investigate their structure. We show that the two-sided structure of $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ is both intricate and well-behaved. Specifically, $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ does not satisfy the ascending chain condition on two-sided ideals, but the two-sided ideals still have a nice structure: there is a canonical nested collection of ideals $I_n$, parameterised by positive integers, so that any nonzero two-sided ideal of $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ contains all $I_n$ for $n \gg 0$. The ideals $I_n$ can be thought of as universal annihilators of natural classes of finite-dimensional representations of $L\mathfrak g$. We also study the Poisson structure of the symmetric algebra $\mathrm{S}(L\mathfrak g)$ and give applications to the representation theory of $L\mathfrak g$.

items.title: Partial Localization and Multifractality in Heterogeneous Population Growth with Resetting
items.summary: We study a model of heterogeneous multiplicative growth with mean-field redistribution and independent local stochastic resetting. The model describes populations or wealth distributed over sites with quenched growth-rate heterogeneity, while resets represent random local extinction or bankruptcy events. At large redistribution or resetting rate, we find a delocalized phase and we compute the growth rate as well as the stationary distribution of the population of a given site. We show that reset-free growth episodes generate power-law stationary tails with site-dependent exponents. For weak resetting and redistribution, favorable sites can undergo long reset-free episodes and localize. This produces a partially localized phase, in which a finite fraction of the total population is carried by a small set of sites whose identity changes on an $O(1)$ time scale within a subextensive pool of $N^{u^\star}$ favorable candidates, with $0<u^\star<1$. We derive the corresponding growth rate from a saddle point analysis, and show that the averaged stationary fractions display multifractal behavior.

items.title: Quality control in sublinear time: a case study via random graphs
items.summary: Many algorithms are designed to work well on average over inputs. But when such an algorithm is run on an arbitrary input, the question arises: Can we trust the algorithm on this input? This question is especially relevant in network science, where algorithms for theoretical random graph models are often applied to individual real-world networks. We identify a new class of algorithmic problems addressing this, which we call "Quality Control Problems." These problems are specified by a "quality function" $ρ$ and a distribution $D$ such that, with high probability, a sample drawn from $D$ is "high quality," meaning its $ρ$-value is near $1$. The goal is to accept most inputs $x \sim D$ and reject potentially adversarially generated inputs $x$ with $ρ(x)$ far from $1$. In this work, we consider the sublinear version of the quality control problem, where $D \in Δ(\{0,1\}^N)$ and the goal is to solve the $(D,ρ)$-quality problem with $o(N)$ queries and time. As a case study, we consider random graphs, i.e., $D = G_{n,p}$ (and $N = \binom{n}2$), and the $k$-clique count function $ρ_k := C_k(G)/\mathbb{E}_{G' \sim G_{n,p}}[C_k(G')]$, where $C_k(G)$ is the number of $k$-cliques in $G$. In suitable parameter ranges, worst-case approximate $k$-clique counting requires $p^{-Ω(k^2)}$ queries. In contrast, we show that the quality control problem for $G_{n,p}$ (with $n\geq p^{-ck}$ for some constant $c$) with respect to $ρ_k$ can be tested with $p^{-O(k)}$ queries and time, showing quality control is provably superpolynomially more efficient in this setting. More generally, for a motif $H$ of maximum degree $Δ(H)$, we show that the corresponding quality control problem can be solved with $p^{-O(Δ(H))}$ queries and running time.

items.title: Ekedahl-Oort strata with a superspecial factor in unitary Shimura varieties
items.summary: Let $\mathbb{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$ and let $O_K$ be an imaginary quadratic order in which $p$ is inert. For any $a,b\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ not both 0, denote by $M(a,b)$ the unitary Shimura variety that parametrizes principally polarized abelian varieties over $\mathbb{k}$ with an action of signature $(a,b)$ by $O_K$ (subject to certain compatibility conditions). For any $a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, there is a natural product map $M(a,b) \times M(c,d) \to M(a+c,b+d)$, which induces a map on Ekedahl-Oort strata. In this paper we focus on product maps where at least one of the factors is superspecial, since most Ekedahl-Oort strata of unitary Shimura varieties contain such a factor. We describe maps with this property completely on the level of Weyl group coset representatives. We also characterize, on the level of Weyl group coset representatives, which Ekedahl-Oort strata of $M(a,b)$ admit a superspecial factor.

items.title: Left properness of Moore flows
items.summary: We introduce reparametrization categories with cuts. For every such category $\mathcal{P}$, the tensor product of two objectwise weak homotopy equivalences of $\mathcal{P}$-spaces is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence, and the q-model structure on $\mathcal{P}$-flows is left proper. The reparametrization categories $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{M}$, as well as the terminal category $\mathbf{1}$, have cuts. The terminal category recovers the left properness of the q-model structure on ordinary flows. We also give a symmetric reparametrization category with cuts and a strict unit. This category is not equivalent to $\mathbf{1}$.

items.title: A non-sober core-compact meet-continuous dcpo
items.summary: We construct a meet-continuous dcpo whose Scott space is core-compact but neither sober nor locally compact. The example is a proper sub-dcpo of a locally compact sober complete lattice, and restriction induces an isomorphism between their lattices of Scott-closed sets. It follows that a locally compact sober dcpo need not be determined, among all dcpos, by its Scott-closed-set lattice.

items.title: Convergence Rates for Lasserre's Upper-Bound Hierarchy on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with Gaussian Measure
items.summary: We establish quantitative convergence rates for Lasserre's measure-based upper-bound hierarchy on $\mathbb{R}^d$ using the standard Gaussian measure as the reference measure. For any polynomial $f$ attaining its global infimum $f_{\min}$, we prove that the order-$r$ upper bounds satisfy $$ λ_r-f_{\min}=O\Big(\frac{1}{r}\Big), $$ yielding, to the best of our knowledge, the first explicit convergence rate for this hierarchy on a noncompact domain. We further show that the rate is sharp by proving an $Ω(1/r)$ rate for $f=x^2$, while demonstrating that, without attainment of the infimum, convergence can be arbitrarily slow: for every $m\ge0$, we construct a polynomial whose upper bounds converge at rate $Θ(r^{-1/(m+2)})$.

items.title: Strongly irreducible operators, $K_0$-groups, and Jones indices in the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor
items.summary: In this paper, we study the strong irreducibility of a class of operators associated with irrational rotation algebras in the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $\mathcal R$. By developing weighted shift models for their relative commutants, we obtain $K_0$ calculations and splitting criteria for direct sums. In particular, we construct strongly irreducible operators in $\mathcal R$ whose relative commutants have $K_0$-groups isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb Z^2$. We realize every Jones index of an irreducible subfactor of $\mathcal R$ as $[\mathcal R:W^*(T)]$ for some strongly irreducible operator $T$ relative to $\mathcal R$. Furthermore, we construct strong generators of $\mathcal R$ and strongly irreducible operators in every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $\mathcal M$ with separable predual.

items.title: Existence and classification of solutions for singular 1-Laplacian equations with gradient terms
items.summary: We study the existence and qualitative properties of non-negative solutions to singular 1-Laplacian problems of the form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -Δ_1 u = g(u)|D u| + h(u)f & \text{in } Ω,\newline u=0 & \text{on } \partialΩ, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, $0<f\in L^{N,\infty}(Ω)$, and $g,h$ are continuous positive functions that may blow up at the origin. We establish the existence of a positive bounded solution even when $g$ is non-integrable at zero and $h(0)=+\infty$, breaking the non-existence phenomenon appearing in the associated $p$-Laplacian problems. Furthermore, we prove that solutions possess a non-zero boundary trace on a set of positive measure of $\partialΩ$ whenever $g(s)$ grows sufficiently fast near $s=0$; by contrast, when this growth condition fails, solutions vanishing on the boundary may appear. Finally, when $h(0)<+\infty$, we provide a sharp threshold classification of trivial and non-trivial solutions depending on the size of $f$.

items.title: On the asymptotic shape of quantile surfaces
items.summary: This article is concerned with the asymptotic shape of quantile surfaces, defined as the set of quantiles at a given level $α$ generated by a controlled one-dimensional distribution. Specifically, when the distribution arises as a linear combination of log-normal random variables and the control is a vector of positive coefficients, we prove that quantile surfaces are globally concave in the left tail ($α\to0$) and globally convex in the right tail ($α\to1$). Moreover, these surfaces exhibit asymptotic separation of scale and shape.

items.title: The asymptotic Erd{ő}s--Frankl--Füredi cover-free conjecture
items.summary: In 1985, Erd{ő}s, Frankl and F{ü}redi conjectured that the threshold $T(r)$ for the existence of an $r$-cover-free family with more members than points satisfies $T(r)=(1+o(1))r^2$. We confirm this conjecture by proving $T(r)\ge r^2+r+2$ for every $r\ge1$.

items.title: Fluctuations from a random fractional averaging limit
items.summary: We consider a system of multiscale stochastic differential equations whose slow component is drivenby a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H greater than 1/2. Under ergodic assumptions ensuring the applicability of the fractional averaging and fractional homogenization theorems of Hairer and Li (arXiv:1902.11251, arXiv:2109.06948), we establish a fluctuation result. The deviation of the slow motion, scaled by epsilon^{1/2-H}, from its effective, time-dependent random limit converges, as the time-separation scale epsilon tends to zero, to the solution of a stochastic differential equation driven by a fractional Brownian motion and influenced by an additional space--time Gaussian field. Since the averaging principle and the fractional homogenization hold in different modes of convergence, obtaining the required joint convergence is a delicate matter. Moreover, neither the continuity of the Ito--Lyons solution map nor the martingale method is directly applicable for our purposes, so the proof requires several innovations. To establish the fluctuation theorem, we combine cumulant methods with a residue lemma and formulate the enlarged system as a rough differential equation in a suitable space.

items.title: Non-Archimedean Poincaré series and geodesics on the Bruhat-Tits tree
items.summary: Adapting a construction of Kurihara in the setting of Drinfeld modular forms, we define Poincaré series on the Drinfeld half-plane $Ω$. These series are built from products of meromorphic $1$-forms that are naturally associated to geodesics on the Bruhat-Tits tree. We establish convergence under a finiteness condition on the geodesics, verify this condition in several cases, and give sufficient conditions for the resulting cusp forms to be nonzero. For the principal congruence subgroup $Γ(\mathfrak{n})$ of $GL_2(\mathbb{F}_q[T])$, we construct explicit linearly independent families of Poincaré series by lifting certain $k$-forms from the components of the analytic reduction of $Γ(\mathfrak{n})\backslashΩ$. We formulate conjectures on the vanishing orders at cusps, and we prove the first of them for an explicit family of Poincaré series by computing the corresponding expansions at the cusps; as an application, we obtain the Drinfeld modular forms $h$ and $Δ$ as Poincaré series (up to a sign). Finally, for cocompact groups attached to quaternion algebras over $\mathbb{F}_q(T)$ that split at $\infty$, we show that the Poincaré series span the whole space of modular forms of given weight and type.

items.title: Schwarz $\mathrm{P}$ and Schwarz $\mathrm{D}$ as free-boundary minimal disks in a tetragonal disphenoid: exact areas
items.summary: Let $T$ be the tetragonal disphenoid whose four congruent faces are isosceles triangles with sides $2,\sqrt3,\sqrt3$, so that the dihedral angles are $π/2$ along one opposite pair of edges and $π/3$ along the remaining four. By Smyth's theorem $T$ contains three embedded minimal disks meeting $\partial T$ orthogonally; the symmetry group $D_{2d}$ of $T$ fixes one and interchanges the other two. We identify all three completely. The distinguished disk is a patch of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{P}$ surface}$ and the congruent pair are patches of $\textbf{Schwarz's $\mathrm{D}$ surface}$, with exact areas \[ \operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{A}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} {K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} = 0.781700961348056\ldots, \] \[ \operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{B}) = \frac{K\!\left(\tfrac34\right)} {2\,K\!\left(\tfrac14\right)} = 0.639630785585503\ldots \] in the normalization $\operatorname{Vol}(T)=2/3$, inradius $r_T=\sqrt2/4$. In particular $2\,\operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{A})\operatorname{Area}(Σ^{*}_{B})=1$, which we show is the Bonnet relation for the adjoint pair $(\mathrm{D},\mathrm{P})$. The proof is a reversal of the usual strategy: rather than uniformizing the Gauss map, we identify Smyth's three Plateau contours as the $\textit{tetrahedral four edges}$ and the $\textit{octahedral four edges}$ --- classically solved by $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ respectively --- and then conjugate. Both areas agree with Surface Evolver computations of Ken Brakke to all $15$ reported digits. We also show that all twelve corners of the three disks are midpoints of edges of $T$, each of the six midpoints being used twice, and that $T$ is precisely the alcove of the affine Weyl group $\widetilde{A}_{3}$, confirming a remark of Gandy, Cvijović, et al. (1999).

items.title: On Stopping Sets and Continuous-Time Decision Trees
items.summary: We study stopping sets and continuous-time decision trees (CTDTs) for Poisson point processes. We first give a proof of the spatial Markov property without assuming that the stopping set contains finitely many points or admits a finite approximation. The proof uses the multivariate Mecke formula on the complement of the stopping set. We then prove that every $μ$-continuous CTDT has an explicit exploration representation: between successive discoveries, the explored set grows according to a deterministic rule depending on the points already observed. If $μ$ is diffuse, the points are revealed one by one almost surely; this need not be imposed as a separate assumption. We also allow atoms of $μ$, in which case all points at one location are revealed together. Finally, for diffuse $μ$, we prove that a locally bounded stopping set revealing at most one point is attainable by a $μ$-continuous exploration. More generally, an increasing sequence of locally bounded stopping sets, each revealing at most one additional point, can be attained by a single exploration at successive stopping times.

items.title: Indiscernible Extraction in Theories with Bounded $k$-splitting
items.summary: Hanson introduced the class of theories with bounded $k$-splitting, a higher-arity notion of stability, and proved an indiscernible extraction result for those theories assuming the existence of a $k$-ineffable cardinal. In this article, we show that the conclusion of Hanson's theorem is equivalent to the weaker assertion that there exists a weakly compact cardinal, as well as prove additional indiscernible extraction results for these theories in ZFC. Finally, we show that Hanson's construction of total bounded ultraimaginary Morley sequences in theories with bounded $k$-splitting follows from ZFC.

items.title: On effective equidistribution for product-type self-affine measures
items.summary: We establish an effective equidistribution theorem on homogeneous spaces for expanding translates of product-type self-affine measures seen on unipotent orbits along any sequence of diagonal elements drifting away from walls. In particular, we do not require the diagonal elements to lie in a fixed proper and closed subcone. The main new ingredients in the proof of our equidistribution theorem include an adaptation of the methods in \cite{BHZ25} to the setting of product-type self-affine measures, as well as a weighted effective recurrence theorem for intertwined associated random walks. The latter involves decomposing the random walks according to suitable stopping times and applications of intertwined Benoist-Quint height functions.

items.title: Plane wave representations for wave scattering on a sphere
items.summary: Motivated by three-dimensional wave diffraction by conical shapes, we consider the two-dimensional problem of wave scattering on the real sphere $\mathcal{S}^2$ resulting from a point-source incidence on a scatterer $\mathbb{S}$. Using the recently introduced notion of plane waves on $\mathcal{S}^2$ as well as recent results on the Laplace--Beltrami Green's function $G$ on $\mathcal{S}^2$, we derive three plane-wave representations for the scattered field $u$. We then explain how $u$ can be analytically continued to the complexified sphere $\mathcal{S}^2_{\mathbb{c}}$. This allows us to formulate a complexified version of Green's third identity, and to provide a characterisation of complex sources. All our results are then used to draw strong analogies between planar and spherical scattering problems, notably through the introduction of directivities.

items.title: Random walk on the small-world network model in 3 or more dimensions
items.summary: We study the mixing time of a simple random walk on the small-world network defined by adding edges to $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ as follows: for each pair $\{x,y\}$ we add an edge with probability $Z_n/\|x-y\|^{d}$ with $Z_n$ chosen so that the average number of added edges to every vertex is $1$. When $d\geq 3$, we show that with high probability the mixing time is of order $\log n$ and that the random walk does not exhibit cutoff.

items.title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
items.summary: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which allows us to derive several new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is either $1$-Frobenius or Burnside.

items.title: Canonical expansions of $\mathbb R_{\mathcal Q}$-germs
items.summary: Let $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ be the field of unary germs at $0^+$ definable in the quasianalytic o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ of Kaiser-Rolin-Speissegger. We construct a canonical ordered differential-field embedding of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ into the field of natural-support generalized Laurent series. Every unary germ has a unique such asymptotic expansion, and bounded germs have expansions with only nonnegative exponents. A germ admits a convergent generalized Laurent-series representation exactly when its canonical expansion converges; in that case, every convergent representation with well-ordered support is canonical. We also prove that $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ is branching in the sense of Dembner [1]. A nonresonant hyperbolic saddle with divergent Dulac series yields a bounded positive real-analytic $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$-definable germ whose canonical generalized power series diverges. This gives a negative answer to a question of Dembner asking whether every unary germ definable in a branching structure admits a convergent generalized power-series representation. Nevertheless, every bounded unary $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$-germ has a canonical formal generalized power-series expansion. Consequently, the convergent germs form a proper ordered differential subfield of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.

items.title: Computing bounded solutions to linear Diophantine equations with the sum of divisors
items.summary: We propose an efficient computational method for finding all solutions $n\leq U$ to the Diophantine equation $aσ(n)=bn+c$, where $a,b,c$ are fixed integer coefficients, $U$ is a given upper bound, and $σ(n)$ denotes the sum of divisors of $n$. The method combines advanced pruning of possible prime factors of $n$ and their combinations with several optimization techniques, organized around a \emph{prime-wheel} data structure developed for this purpose. It is implemented in the {\sc SageMath} computer algebra system within the framework of recursively enumerated sets and supports native {\sc MapReduce} parallelization. We apply the method to numerous previously studied equations, discovering new solutions, certifying complete solution lists below substantially larger bounds than previously reported, and substantially improving lower bounds in several open problems involving the sum-of-divisors function.

items.title: The chain replacement of a poset flow
items.summary: We introduce the chain replacement of a poset flow: it is obtained by considering the simplicial nerves of the posets of strictly increasing chains in the given poset, ordered by refinement. It maps posets to q-cofibrant flows and inclusions of posets to q-cofibrations. Using the combinatorial properties of the chain replacement, we prove that pushouts along the chain replacement of an order-reflecting inclusion of posets induce trivial h-cofibrations on spaces of execution paths between states of the original flow. By introducing the Hurewicz model structure on flows (or H-model structure), we deduce the same property for any q-cofibrant replacement of an order-reflecting inclusion of posets.

items.title: Robustness for free: asymptotic size and power of max-tests in high dimensions
items.summary: Allowing for adversarial contamination and heavy tails, we study testing whether the mean of a high-dimensional random vector equals zero. Because standard max-tests based on sample averages are highly non-robust, we propose a max-test based on quantile-winsorized observations. The test controls asymptotic size under adversarial contamination and only requires $m>2$ moments, while allowing dimension to grow exponentially with sample size. We fully characterize its asymptotic power function. Comparing with the standard max-test, for which we also derive a power characterization as a benchmark, we show that robustness is obtained for free at first order: under the stronger conditions that make the standard max-test valid, our robust test has identical asymptotic power. We show that the decay condition on the contamination-rate imposed is necessary for this no-first-order-loss property. Finally, we also study the role of bootstrap critical values, showing that their use never decreases power, can strictly improve asymptotic power in extremely correlated designs, but often has no first-order asymptotic effect.

items.title: Boundary geometry and concentration points for attractive Bose-Einstein condensates with a ring-shaped potential
items.summary: In this paper, we study the ground states of attractive Bose-Einstein condensates in a bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb R^2$ under the ring-shaped trapping potential $$ V(x)=(|x|-1)^2. $$ The boundary geometry of $Ω$ may allow the ring $Γ=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:|x|=1\}$ of global minima for $V(x)$ to meet both the interior and the boundary of $Ω$. As the interaction strength approaches the critical value, we prove that if $Γ\cap Ω\not=\emptyset$, the mass of ground states concentrates at a point $x_0\inΓ\cap Ω$ that has maximal distance from $\partialΩ$. Our method relies on exponential upper and lower bounds for the difference between the bounded domain and whole space minimal energies. The essential lower bound follows from a uniform quadratic-growth estimate near the ground state manifold of the whole space problem, which is established by combining the nondegeneracy of the optimizer for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality with a Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction.

items.title: LGNO: A Local-Global Neural Operator for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
items.summary: Solutions of hyperbolic conservation laws exhibit both smooth structures across large scales and sharp localized features such as shocks and contact discontinuities, making them difficult to approximate accurately with existing neural operators. The Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) captures long-range interactions well but tends to smear localized structures through excessive numerical dissipation. To address this, we propose a Local-Global Neural Operator (LGNO) that learns a one-step discrete flow map by combining a global FNO branch for representing smooth dynamics at large scales with a local multiresolution branch for enhancing localized discontinuities and nonsmooth features. The model is trained with a one-step loss that combines a physical space prediction term and a spectral penalty on high frequencies to suppress spurious oscillations near steep fronts. On a large collection of benchmarks in one and two dimensions, LGNO consistently outperforms FNO baselines with matched parameter counts, reducing one-step errors by factors of 2-5 and remaining significantly more accurate over long autoregressive rollouts. Most strikingly, although it is trained only on short-time data from a high-order WENO-Z scheme, the long-time rollout of LGNO on a coarse $256^2$ grid exhibits lower numerical dissipation than the same WENO-Z scheme run on a finer $512^2$ grid, while being orders of magnitude cheaper to evaluate. These results suggest that, with an appropriate architecture and training objective, learned operators can effectively learn discrete flow maps. They further suggest that such learned operators have the potential to control long-time numerical dissipation better than the conventional shock-capturing schemes that generate the training data.

items.title: A Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Time-Modulated Drude--Lorentz Media
items.summary: We formulate and analyze a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for Maxwell's equations coupled to four time-modulated Drude--Lorentz models: modulated in-coupling, modulated polarization density, modulated current density, and modulated effective mass. The use of electric displacement and model-dependent continuous material states gives a common treatment of temporal interfaces while preserving the distinct physical transmission rules. We derive energy and stability estimates, establish spatial and event-aligned time-error bounds, and separate time-integration error from error caused by misplaced switching times. Numerical experiments in three dimensions and in reduced modal systems confirm the predicted spatial, temporal, and switch-timing behavior, including the field-jump effect specific to the polarization-density model.

items.title: Principal component error in high-dimensional factor models
items.summary: In a statistical factor model, principal components (or eigenvectors) of a sample covariance matrix serve as estimates of principal directions, the true drivers of co-movement of a collection of observed variables. We write the often substantial error in these estimates as a sum of two interpretable terms, which we show have almost sure asymptotic limits as the number of variables grows with sample size bounded. This scenario is commonplace in financial economics, genomics, machine learning and signal processing. Out-of-subspace error measures the distance from an estimate to the subspace spanned by population factor exposures. It can be expressed in terms of data, providing an estimable floor for asymptotic error. In-subspace error is driven by a rotation error within that subspace, which arises from the fixed sample size of the latent factor returns and cannot be estimated from data alone. We illustrate our error analysis with a three-factor simulation of the US public equity market, showing the dependence of the magnitude of the error and its components on dimension and sample size. In that simulation, out-of-subspace error dominates. Researchers who rely on principal component analysis to estimate factor models can use our results to quantify errors in model-based predictions and attributions.

items.title: Counting rational points on non-uniruled surfaces
items.summary: Let $X\subseteq \mathbb{P}^n$ be a non-degenerate non-uniruled irreducible projective surface of degree $d$ defined over a number field $K$, and let $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)$ be the number of rational points of $X$ of height at most $B$ that do not lie on lines contained in $X$. Assuming a suitable hypothesis on the size of the rank of Abelian varieties, we show that $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)\ll_{K,n,d,\varepsilon}B^{\frac{n+1}{n}+\varepsilon}$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$. In particular, if $X\subseteq \mathbb{P}^3$ is a smooth projective surface of degree $d\ge 4$ defined over a number field $K$, then $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)\ll_{K,d,\varepsilon} B^{4/3+\varepsilon}$. This conditionally improves a bound of Salberger for $d=4$ and $d=5$. The proof, based on an argument of Heath-Brown, consists of cutting $X$ by projective hyperplanes and using a uniform version of Faltings's Theorem, due to Dimitrov, Gao, and Habegger, to bound the number of rational points on the hyperplane sections of $X$.

items.title: Finite Cumulant Towers for Small-System-Noise Expansions in Nonlinear Filtering
items.summary: We study asymptotic expansions for nonlinear filtering in the small-system-noise regime. Our main result is that the expansion coefficients of conditional cumulants satisfy a closed finite-dimensional system that can be solved recursively. At each expansion degree, the evolution of a coefficient introduces a coefficient of the next higher cumulant rank, while a high-rank vanishing property terminates this hierarchy, yielding a finite triangular tower. The first layer is the Kalman--Bucy filter, and subsequent layers satisfy linear equations once the lower layers are known. To derive these equations, we establish generalized Zakai and Kushner--Stratonovich equations for observation-dependent random variables and obtain explicit coefficient equations in arbitrary dimension. The conditional cumulant expansion also determines the expansion of the conditional characteristic function. We further obtain an explicit bound on the number of scalar variables in terms of the state dimension and expansion degree. When the observation function vanishes, the construction reduces to ODEs for unconditional cumulant coefficients. Comparisons with existing asymptotic-expansion algorithms illustrate the resulting reduction in the number of ODE variables.

items.title: The linear independence of $1$, $ζ(3)$, and $ζ(4)$
items.summary: In a recent breakthrough, Fauzan proved the irrationality of $ζ(5)$. In this paper, we combine Fauzan's determinant method with classical simultaneous approximations of zeta values studied by Zudilin and Dauguet--Zudilin to prove the linear independence of $1$, $ζ(3)$, and $ζ(4)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. As a corollary, $ζ(3)/π^4$ is irrational.

items.title: Deep Learning of Topological Equivalence Classes
items.summary: We demonstrate an application of deep learning to the problem of identifying whether two generating vectors correspond to topologically equivalent finite group actions on Riemann surfaces, showing how architectures developed for semantic understanding have use for pure mathematical problems. In doing so we discuss how desired algebraic structure influences model design, and explore which structural properties of topological equivalence classes the model has successfully learnt.

items.title: Mixing time of the lazy and simple random walk on a randomly twisted hypercube
items.summary: We consider a randomly twisted hypercube on $N$ vertices and study a simple or lazy random walk on this graph. We show that for both walks the mixing time is of order $\log N$, and the model does not exhibit cutoff. We also establish that both walks have cover time of order $N\log N$, and we show that the chromatic number of the graph diverges.

items.title: Sharp Cramér-type moderate deviation bounds for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums
items.summary: Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d. random variables with zero mean and variance $σ^2\in(0,\infty)$. In this paper, we establish a sharp Cramér-type moderate deviation for the self-normalized maximum of partial sums under a finite $p$-th absolute moment, $2<p\le3$. In particular, we show that $\mathbb{P}(M_n\ge xV_n)=2(1-Φ(x))\{1+O(1)β_{n,p}(1+x)^p\}$ for $0\le x\leβ_{n,p}^{-1/p}$, where $M_n=\max_{1\le k\le n}\sum_{j=1}^kX_j$, $V_n=(\sum_{j=1}^nX_j^2)^{1/2}$, $β_{n,p}=\mathbb{E}|X_1|^p/(n^{(p-2)/2}σ^p)$, and $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. This proves a conjecture of Shao2010. More precisely, we bound the relative error by the same truncated-moment quantity as for self-normalized sums. The proof compares the maximum with the absolute sum while preserving their common denominator, through a reflected-walk representation and Fourier estimates with distribution-adapted smoothing.

items.title: Conditioning diffusions on a terminal bearing
items.summary: We study sampling of a diffusion on $[0,T]$ conditioned on its terminal position lying on a prescribed ray, i.e. on an exactly observed bearing. For a linear drift we derive closed-form expressions for the Doob $h$-function and its gradient. For a broad class of tracking models admitting a Kronecker block structure, the guiding term is obtained from a single row of a matrix exponential, and the conditioned process decomposes into independent radial and angular components. For a nonlinear drift, we construct a guided process using the $h$-function of the linear model and prove absolute continuity of the law of the true conditioned process with respect to the law of the guided process, with an explicit likelihood ratio. This result is used to devise an auxiliary particle filter for bearings observed sequentially in time without noise. Numerical experiments show that the proposed filter approximates the filtering distribution and estimates the log-likelihood considerably more accurately than the shifted Rayleigh filter, at the cost of a higher computing time.

items.title: Schur positivity of the lattices $\mathbf m\times\mathbf n$
items.summary: We prove that the product of chains $\mathbf m\times\mathbf n$ is not Schur positive whenever $n\ge4$ and $m\ge3n-1$. Writing $m=n+k$, we exhibit a negative Schur coefficient indexed by $(2n+k-1,2n+k-3,\ldots,k+5,k,k,4)$ and evaluate it explicitly as $(n-2)!$ times a polynomial of degree three in $k$. Together with earlier results, this establishes the two-case interpretation of the conjecture of Li, Qiu, Yang, and Zhang: these products are not Schur positive when $n=2$ and $m\ge8$, or when $n\ge3$ and $m\ge n+5$.

items.title: Discrete Temporal CSPs et al
items.summary: We revisit the complexity classification of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) for first-order reducts of $(\mathbb{Z},<)$, established by Bodirsky, Martin, and Mottet in 2018. Following their approach, we give a self-contained proof of this classification, correcting several errors in the argument. We further show that, with the exception of cases arising from finite-domain CSPs, all tractable cases are solved by a well-known uniform algorithm, eliminating the need for the collection of ad-hoc algorithms used in the original paper. A central component of the proof allows the analysis to be restricted to first-order reducts of $(\mathbb{Z},<)$ that contain the successor relation. We substantially simplify this reduction and generalize the underlying construction. This generalization allows us to apply the same technique to first-order reducts of the triangular lattice graph and of infinite regular trees, yielding a complete complexity classification for these classes of structures, in particular a $\mathsf{P}$ versus $\mathsf{NP}$-complete dichotomy.

items.title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
items.summary: Neural networks often learn low-frequency components before high-frequency ones --- a phenomenon called spectral bias or termed F-principle. Many numerical studies have demonstrated this phenomenon, and theoretical studies have sought to explain it. However, several goals remain insufficiently addressed: (1) explaining spectral bias asymptotically, including its origin and why the preferred components are generally sinusoidal; (2) extending the explanation to general activation functions, such as sigmoid and ReLU; (3) making weak assumptions about the data distribution; (4) avoiding aliasing effects, such as those arising in finite-domain Fourier analysis; and (5) developing a theoretical framework applicable to arbitrary networks. We address these goals theoretically by analyzing the eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes of the dynamics matrix H, which arises when we expand the network output as a general Fourier series (GFS) in an orthogonal polynomial basis and express the gradient-descent dynamics of the GFS coefficients as ordinary differential equations. The graded structure of H enables an intuitive explanation of spectral bias, while orthogonal polynomial theory helps us analyze how learning bias depends on the activation function and, potentially, the network architecture.

items.title: Singular Yamabe metrics on complements of closed sets
items.summary: Let $n\geq3$ and let $Λ\subset \mathbb S^n$ be closed, contain at least two points, and satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm H}Λ<(n-2)/2$. We prove that there exists a complete metric of scalar curvature $n(n-1)$ on $\mathbb S ^n\setminusΛ$, conformal to the round metric.

items.title: The derived category of a generalized complex torus
items.summary: For any translation invariant generalized complex structure J on a torus we construct the derived category D(J) generalizing the derived category of coherent sheaves on a complex torus and the affine/convergent Fukaya category of a symplectic torus. The category is defined in terms of a non-commutative curved deformation of the Dolbeault algebra of a complex torus. We show that this category is independent of the chosen deformation path, which we prove using non-commutative Fourier-Mukai duality. We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).

items.title: Non-convex polytopes realizing kissing contact graphs in dimensions 5-7
items.summary: Each of the 12 known conjecturally optimal kissing configurations in dimensions 5, 6, and 7 carries a contact-graph polytope: a polytope whose vertices are the configuration points and whose edges are exactly its contacts. Eight of these polytopes are non-convex and distinct from their convex hulls, which include longer edges. Each polytope is radial about the sphere's center: its boundary meets every ray from the center exactly once. It is the unique radial polytope with those vertices and edges. Seven of the nine non-lattice configurations carry polytopes constructed from the lattice contact polytope in the same dimension by splitting some facets and reassembling the pieces. This split-and-reassemble construction describes the configurations by facets rather than by layers. The fold angles of the reassembled facets explain the inner products $1/(10-n)$, giving $1/5$, $1/4$, and $1/3$ in dimensions 5, 6, and 7, respectively. The contact graphs of all 12 configurations are infinitesimally rigid. We also prove that $Q_5$ and $R_5$ are infinitesimally jammed, extending the 10 previously established cases to all 12 configurations. All mathematical computations use exact arithmetic.

items.title: Mod 3 Congruence Families for twisted signatures of string manifolds in dimensions up to twenty-eight
items.summary: In the paper, we establish congruences for twisted Dirac indices and signatures on closed string manifolds by specializing the two-parameter modular forms of Liu and Wang to the tangent bundle. Fourier coefficient comparisons yield uniform congruences modulo $3$ in dimensions $4k$, $1\leq k\leq7$. Suitable parameter choices give explicit formulas involving only genuine twisting bundles in dimensions $8,12,16,20,24,$ and $28$, and recover the comparisons of Chen and Han in dimension $24$. The level-one Witten genus further strengthens selected Dirac congruences to moduli $729,27,27,$ and $9$ in dimensions $16,20,24,$ and $28$, respectively. The proofs use Fourier expansions in reduced $K$-theory and integer identities obtained by clearing powers of two from the denominators before reduction modulo $3$. We also construct non-string spin counterexamples in each of the six listed dimensions and identify the additional coefficient that obstructs extending the uniform argument to dimension $32$ without further information.

items.title: Computational Models for Magnetic Drug Targeting, Part 1: Derivation and Numerical Simulation of a Thermodynamically Consistent Magneto Two-phase Flow Model
items.summary: Motivated by Magnetic Drug Targeting (MDT), we derive a thermodynamically consistent two-phase model for the coupled dynamics of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs), a carrier fluid, and the magnetic field. The model includes a convection-diffusion equation for the SPION dispersion volume density and a modified Navier-Stokes system for the mixture velocity with SPION-dependent density and viscosity, an additional momentum flux due to relative SPION motion, and a magnetic body force. Additionally, the SPIONs interact with a quasi-static Maxwell system through their magnetization which is of Langevin type. The coupled system satisfies a global energy-dissipation balance. Moreover, we develop a semi-implicit finite element scheme with explicit flux-corrected transport stabilization and simulate the attraction of an initially localized SPION dispersion towards an external magnet in a system closed to mass exchange, using parameter values representative of MDT settings. The resulting SPION redistribution and induced flow are analyzed through physical observables, including energy and dissipation contributions and iron mass within a target region. Temporal convergence studies assess the ability of the numerical scheme to reproduce the energy-dissipation balance. Finally, we study the influence of individual coupling mechanisms on particle accumulation, maximum iron density, and peak flow velocity.

items.title: Sharp Hessian integrability for the planar Monge--Ampère equation
items.summary: We determine the optimal local integrability of the Hessian for planar convex Alexandrov solutions satisfying $$ λ\,dx\leqμ_u\leqλ^{-1}\,dx, \qquad 0<λ<1. $$ The distributional Hessian satisfies the sharp endpoint estimate $$ D^2u\in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{P,\infty}, \qquad P=\frac{1+λ}{1-λ}. $$ This settles the weak estimate proposed by De Philippis and Figalli and identifies the larger optimal exponent $P$. We further construct strictly convex $C^1$ solutions for which the distribution function of the Laplacian is comparable to $T^{-P}$ for all sufficiently large $T$. Hence both the exponent and the weak Lorentz endpoint are optimal: $L^{P,\infty}$ cannot be replaced by $L^{P,b}$ for any finite $b>0$. As applications, we obtain sharp estimates in Minty coordinates and optimal quantitative bi-Lipschitz restrictions for gradient maps, including an optimal exceptional-mass bound in quadratic-cost transport.

items.title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
items.summary: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.

items.title: Postnikov invariants for rational spaces
items.summary: In this paper we construct a theory of Postnikov invariants for (complete) homotopy Lie algebras that is preserved by the integration functor of Robert-Nicoud and Vallette. This result is in the same vein as Berglund's theorem, which relates the homology groups underlying a nilpotent homotopy Lie algebra to the homotopy groups of the associated space. We then deduce an integration functor from filtered Chevalley-Eilenberg homology groups to group cohomology groups.

items.title: On the Sampling of Certain Dirichlet and Prime Sums at Gram Points and their Viscosity
items.summary: Consider the Dirichlet polynomial and its prime-indexed sub-sum \[ \begin{array}{ccc} E(t) := \sum_{k\le \left[ \sqrt{ \frac{t}{2π} } \right]} \frac{e^{it\log k}}{\sqrt{k}}, & ; & E_1(t) := \sum_{\substack{p\le \left[ \sqrt{\frac{t}{2π}} \right]\\ p\ {\rm prime}}} \frac{e^{it\log p}}{\sqrt p}. \end{array} \] In this work we investigate the statistical and arithmetic properties of the sets \[ \mathcal{C}_N := \left\{ E(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \qquad \mathcal{P}_N := \left\{ E_1(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \] obtained by sampling these sums at the Gram points \(g_n\) of the Hardy \(Z\)-function. We refer to \(\mathcal{C}_N\) and \(\mathcal{P}_N\) as the full and prime \(N\)-th Gram clouds, respectively. The motivation is that the approximate functional equation expresses both \(Z(g_n)\) and \(Z'(g_n)\) through different projections of the same oscillatory phase configuration, suggesting that the geometry of these sampled sums may retain information about the local behavior of nearby zeros. Numerically, we find that Gram-point sampling produces highly non-generic geometric structures: good and isolated bad Gram points occupy markedly different regions of the clouds, the prime cloud of isolated bad points splits into two anisotropic lobes, and the position along the principal direction of the folded prime cloud is strongly correlated with the viscosity of the Hardy $Z$-function \( μ(g_n)=\left|\frac{Z'(g_n)}{Z(g_n)}\right|, \) with smallest-viscosity points concentrating near distinguished extremal regions of the lobes.

items.title: Robust Parallel Machine Scheduling: A Comparison of Robustness Measures and Local Search Approaches
items.summary: In many real-world scheduling problems, the processing times of tasks are subject to uncertainty. This makes it essential to design schedules that are robust against disruptions. We distinguish between two types of robustness: quality-robust schedules keep a stable objective value under disruptions, while solution-robust schedules keep a stable schedule structure. We study how to generate schedules for the Stochastic Parallel Machine Scheduling Problem (SPMSP) with precedence constraints and release dates that are both quality- and solution-robust. To this end, we compare several robustness measures and local search algorithms that use these measures. We start with an extensive simulation study where we determine the correlation of 13 existing and 6 new robustness measures with both quality and solution robustness. Next, we use the measures with high robustness correlation as the objective in our local search algorithm to find the best way to generate schedules containing both job-machine assignments as well as buffer assignments. We use a new dynamic objective weight within our local search algorithms, which actively changes the objective weights in each iteration. We found that the best way to generate robust schedules is to use robustness measures that model the processing times with normal distribution approximations and to combine job placement and buffer assignment simultaneously.

items.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on abelian Cayley graphs
items.summary: We completely classify connected Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups that exhibit perfect state transfer in Grover walks. First, we show that a Cayley graph over any finite group exhibiting perfect state transfer has valency $1$, $2$, or $4$. For valency $4$, we prove that an abelian Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $S=\{a,-a,a+h,-a+h\}$, where $h$ has order $2$, and $4\nmid |Γ|/2$. Combining this characterization with the valency-one and valency-two cases, we explicitly determine all pairs $(Γ,S)$ for which $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer. Our results extend the classification of circulant graphs of valency at most four obtained by Kubota and Yoshino [Circulant graphs with valency up to 4 that admit perfect state transfer in Grover walks, \emph{J. Comb. Theory Ser. A.}, 216 (2025) 106064] to Cayley graphs over arbitrary finite abelian groups and to all valencies.

items.title: Uniformization of Julia sets of geometrically finite rational maps
items.summary: A Schottky set is the complement of a collection of disjoint open disks in the Riemann sphere. We completely characterize geometrically finite rational maps whose Julia sets are quasiconformally equivalent to Schottky sets. We also prove that the closure of the basin of infinity of a geometrically finite unicritical polynomial is quasiconformally equivalent to a Schottky set if and only if either there exists an attracting cycle and all bounded Fatou components have disjoint closures or there exists a parabolic cycle of multiplicity three. An ingredient of the proof is a new dynamical characterization of pairs of arbitrary quasicircles that are quasiconformally equivalent to pairs of tangent circles.

items.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
items.summary: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $Γ$ satisfies $\exp(Γ) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.

items.title: The Orbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial
items.summary: We introduce the \emph{orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial}, which counts generalized vertex colorings of a graph up to the action of a group of symmetries. More precisely, adjacent vertices must either receive distinct colors from a set of $λ$ colors or may receive the same color from a distinguished subset of $λ-μ$ colors. This new graph polynomial simultaneously generalizes the orbital chromatic polynomial due to Cameron and Kayibi (2007) and bivariate chromatic polynomial due to Dohmen, Pönitz, and Tittmann (2003). We establish fundamental structural properties and derive explicit formulas for several graph families, including complete graphs, complete bipartite graphs, paths, cycles, and wheels. In particular, several of these results are new even in the special case of the orbital chromatic polynomial. For cycles, our results generalize Moreau's necklace polynomial and lead to a new generalization and proof of Fermat's Little Theorem.

items.title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
items.summary: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework in which a system designer leverages knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix $G^*$. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh attack environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

items.title: Gromov-Hausdorff Convergence of Constant Scalar Curvature Kähler Metrics near the Canonical Class
items.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-ample canonical bundle. For any Kähler class $[ω]$, Jian--Shi--Song proved that there exists a unique cscK metric in the class $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ when $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0]$, using the properness criterion of Chen--Cheng. We prove that the cscK metrics in $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ converge, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology to the metric completion of the twisted Kähler-Einstein metric on the canonical model of $X$ as conjectured by Jian--Shi--Song. Based on the technique developed in this paper, we can also give a new proof the theorem of Lee--Tosatti--Zhang on the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of the normalized Kähler--Ricci flow on $X$.

items.title: Explicit Ricci-flat metrics on a special Schoen threefold
items.summary: We give an explicit convergent representation of the Ricci-flat Kähler metric in a one-parameter family of classes on a fixed special Schoen threefold. The threefold resolves a shifted square-torus quotient with sixteen disjoint elliptic singular curves. Radial Eguchi--Hanson product metrics and fixed flat collars define a positive background with an exact $a^4$ volume defect. Spherical harmonics, tangential Fourier modes, Frobenius recurrences, radial ordered integrals, and the flat quotient heat kernel specify the inverse of the background scalar linearized operator. A boundary transmission series has contraction factor $1/15$. Independent weighted zeroth-order and six-dimensional Schauder estimates give the inverse bound needed for the quadratic and cubic Monge--Ampère terms. The resulting source-degree recursion converges for $0<a\le2^{-2260}$, with explicit coefficient, potential-tail, and relative metric-tail bounds. The representation uses specified kernels, prescribed integrals, and convergent series; its parameter interval is a sufficient quantitative bound on this fixed model.

items.title: Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
items.summary: We initiate a theory of ``operator spaces" (in other words subspaces of $C^*$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity problems.This first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^*$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one. This also characterizes the $M$'s such that all completely bounded derivations into $M$ are inner. Our main tool for this is a new characterization of injective von Neumann algebras.

items.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
items.summary: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

items.title: An introduction to algebraic groups
items.summary: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.

items.title: On a conjecture of King-Tollu-Toumazet for rectangular Kostka coefficients
items.summary: A conjecture of King, Tollu and Toumazet predicts the behavior of small Littlewood--Richardson coefficients under stretching: if $c^ν_{λ,μ}=3$, then $c^{Mν}_{Mλ,Mμ}$ equals $2M+1$ or $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for every positive integers $M$. This corresponds to the Hilbert functions of a conic, or of the projective plane. We prove their conjecture for all rectangular Kostka coefficients $K_{λ,\mathbf{a}}$. We realize them as the weight multiplicities of the homogeneous coordinate ring of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$, or equivalently the weight spaces of semi-invariants of the $n$-subspace quiver with dimension vector $β=(k,1,1,\dotsc,1)$. For a weight $σ$, we show that if $β$ is $σ$-stable, then the dimension of the corresponding weight space is at least $n-2$ when $k=2$ and at least $4$ for every Grassmannian other than $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$. These three cases are precisely when the associated moduli space of $σ$-stable representations has dimension at most two. Via $σ$-stable decomposition, the two alternatives are determined as follows: $2M+1$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, and $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$.

items.title: A variation on local trilinear form
items.summary: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field and $M$ the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2^3(F)$ consisting of triples with equal determinants. For each unitary principal series $L$-packet of $M$ whose central character is trivial on the diagonal $F^\times$, we determine its unique member distinguished by the diagonal $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$.

items.title: Minimum nonlinearity for pattern-forming Turing instability in a mathematical autocatalytic model
items.summary: Pattern formation is ubiquitous in nature and the mechanism widely-accepted to underlay them is based on the Turing instability, predicted by Alan Turing decades ago. This is a non-trivial mechanism that involves nonlinear interaction terms between the different species involved and transport mechanisms. We present here a mathematical analysis aiming to explore the mathematical constraints that a reaction-diffusion dynamical model should comply in order to exhibit a Turing instability. The main conclusion limits the existence of this instability to nonlinearity degrees larger or equal to three.

items.title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret
items.summary: Many modern learning systems are used not to select a single best action, but to sample diverse high-quality outputs. Examples include entropy-regularized reinforcement learning, RLHF, and reward-guided generative modeling. Motivated by these settings, we study tilted sampling: an online learning problem in which the goal is to sample from the Gibbs distribution induced by an unknown reward function. We define sampling regret as the temperature-normalized cumulative KL divergence between the learner's distribution and the Gibbs target, corresponding to the suboptimality gap in entropy-regularized reward maximization. Our framework generalizes recent sampling-based and KL-regularized formulations in bandits and reinforcement learning. Our main contribution is a general regret framework that captures the different uncertainty structure of tilted sampling and classical regret minimization. While standard regret scales as $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ due to first-order uncertainty, sampling regret is governed by squared confidence widths, yielding logarithmic-in-$T$ regret in standard settings at fixed temperature. We develop sampling analogues of UCB and Thompson sampling (UCS and TS$^2$) and provide unified regret decompositions that explain and extend recent logarithmic guarantees, including the first Bayesian sampling-regret decomposition based on new bounds for posterior-random Gibbs distributions. Our results show that learning to sample from a soft-optimal distribution is statistically distinct from learning to identify a hard optimum.

items.title: Extended Frege proofs, circuits and rewriting
items.summary: Inspired by a statement about Extended Frege proof systems by Jain and Jin (FOCS 2022) we prove that: - there is a p-time binary relation $\approx$ between circuits that implies their logical equivalence, - if the equivalence $C \equiv D$ has an Extended Frege or a Circuit Frege proof with $k$ steps then there is a chain of circuits $E_i$ $$ C = E_0 \approx \dots \approx E_t = D $$ with $t \le O(k \log k)$, and the total size of the chain is bounded above by $(k+|C|+|D|)^{O(1)}$.

items.title: Reconstruction of Fano manifolds from the orthogonal to an exceptional vector bundle
items.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth complex Fano manifolds of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundles and let $V_X$ and $V_Y$ be exceptional vector bundles on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. We prove that a Fourier--Mukai equivalence $V_X^\perp\simeq V_Y^\perp$ implies $X\simeq Y$.

items.title: Local Convexity and Planarity Estimates for Mean Curvature Flow
items.summary: We establish local convexity and cylindrical pinching estimates for hypersurface mean curvature flow under an intermediate convexity condition and integral bounds on the mean curvature. These estimates hold after a positive waiting time and do not require pointwise upper bounds for the mean curvature on the parabolic boundary. In arbitrary codimension, we also establish local planarity estimates for properly defined flows satisfying a uniform $c_n$-pinching condition, without assuming bounded curvature. As applications, the hypersurface estimates yield convexity and cylindrical pinching for complete, spacetime-proper ancient hypersurface flows with uniform Euclidean area growth, without any bounded-curvature assumption. The planarity estimates imply that every complete, connected, spacetime-proper ancient flow satisfying the uniform $c_n$-pinching condition is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-plane for all time.

items.title: Isaac's Condition (TU) is false
items.summary: In 2006 Isaac reduced the simple normality to base $2$ of $\sqrt s$, for $s$ not a perfect square, to a property of dyadic expansions that he called Condition~(TU): the upper frequency of the digit~$1$ in $\sqrtν$, along any subsequence, depends only on the tail of the expansion of $ν$. We show that Condition~(TU) is false, already for the full sequence. We give two proofs. The first is elementary and turns Isaac's own reduction against the condition. The second uses the theorem of Kaufman and Mosquera--Shmerkin on the Fourier decay of smooth images of self-similar measures, and gives counterexamples for almost every point of a Cantor measure.
