The bounds are given in terms of the Bang degree determined by the weight sequence $M$, the degree $d$, and the norming constant of $Γ(f)$ with respect to the space of real bivariate polynomials of degree at most $d$. We give instances, where the bounds are at most polynomial in $d$ and, consequently, the graph $Γ(f)$ contains few rational points: the number of rational points of height at most $H$ is bounded by a polynomial in $\log H$.

items.title: Higher Verlinde categories of reductive groups
items.summary: We define tensor categories ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}(G)$ in characteristic $p$ for connected reductive groups $G$ and positive integers $n$, generalising the semisimple Verlinde categories ${\sf Ver}_p(G)$ originating from Gelfand-Kazhdan and the higher Verlinde categories ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}$ for ${\rm SL}_2$ defined by Benson-Etingof-Ostrik. The construction is based on the definition of ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}$ as an abelian envelope of a quotient of a category of tilting modules, but we also introduce an expanded construction which refines the ${\rm SL}_2$ case and gives new results. In particular, the union ${\sf Ver}_{p^\infty}(G)$ can be derived from the perfection of $G$; certain exact sequences in ${\sf Rep}G$ map to exact sequences in ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}(G)$; and the underlying abelian category of ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}$ can be expressed as a subcategory of ${\sf Rep}{\rm SL}_2$, or as a Serre quotient of a subcategory of ${\sf Rep}{\rm SL}_2$.

items.title: Graphs with three eigenvalues from group divisible designs
items.summary: We construct biregular graphs with three distinct eigenvalues from semiregular group divisible designs. For every prime power $q$, we use the spectral structure of Muzychuk's Construction~A on $q+1$ copies of $\operatorname{AG}(2,q^2)$ to produce suitable group divisible designs. The resulting biregular graphs have $2q^5+q^4+q^2$ vertices and distinct eigenvalues $q^5+q^3+q^2$, $q^2$, and $-q^2$. Their coherent closures have rank $12$ and type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&5\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. We also determine the four-class symmetric association schemes that are the coherent closures of the auxiliary graphs in this family. Computational searches provide further graphs on $81$ and $156$ vertices, using Muzychuk's Construction~B and a generalised quadrangle, respectively; their coherent closures have ranks $13$ and $10$. The $156$-vertex example has a strongly regular design as its coherent closure, of type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&3\end{smallmatrix}\right]$, answering a question of the authors. We also realise a $126$-vertex example by switching a strongly regular graph.

items.title: Worst-Case and Covariance-Reconstruction Robust Adaptive Beamforming: Equivalence and Closed-Form Solution
items.summary: Robust adaptive beamforming (RAB) has developed along two separate lines. The worst-case-constrained approach guards against steering vector mismatch with a bounded uncertainty set, but suffers from desired signal cancellation at high input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The covariance-reconstruction approach instead estimates the interference-plus-noise covariance matrix and solves for the mismatch numerically. We prove that the two are related by primal-dual equivalence: once the worst-case beamformer is normalized, it coincides exactly with the reconstruction-based one, so both reduce to one formulation. The signal cancellation of the worst-case approach is a consequence of its parameter choice, not of the formulation. For the unified problem we develop a closed-form solution in three stages: Diagonalization Transform, Phase Alignment, and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) Solution. Instead of solving for the Lagrange multiplier, we introduce an auxiliary variable that reduces the KKT system to a single scalar equation solvable by bisection. For an $N$-sensor array the cost is $\mathcal{O}(N^{3})$, the same order as the Lagrange-equation-based RMVB and well below the $\mathcal{O}(N^{3.5})$ of a second-order cone program, and it covers the rank-deficient case that RMVB excludes. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for existence and uniqueness, including a case where the feasible set is nonempty yet no optimal solution exists, and show that the Lagrange multiplier fixes the optimal value. Simulations confirm that, with matching parameters, the worst-case beamformer attains the output signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of the reconstruction-based one, and that the closed-form solution reproduces the optimum of convex solvers in a fraction of their time.

items.title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
items.summary: Steady solutions at high Reynolds numbers are computed using an iterative method that linearizes the nonlinear convective terms. This linearization reduces the original nonlinear boundary-value problem to a sequence of linear problems, one solved at each iteration, thereby improving the numerical robustness of the algorithm and enabling convergence over a wide range of governing parameters. The stability of steady incompressible fluid flows is studied within the framework of a linear problem for perturbations. The original steady velocity and pressure fields are subjected to small perturbations, after which the equations are linearized with respect to the perturbations. The resulting linear problem allows one to analyze the evolution of small perturbations and to establish whether the steady solutions under consideration are stable with respect to infinitesimal perturbations. In this work, the computational implementation is based on spatial discretization by the finite element method on triangular meshes. The stability of the obtained solutions is analyzed by solving a generalized algebraic eigenvalue problem formed after discretization of the linear problem for perturbations. The presence of eigenvalues with positive real part indicates instability, whereas their absence indicates stability. Calculations were performed on a sequence of refined meshes at various Reynolds numbers for the flow in a square cavity.

items.title: The $L\log L$-Luxemburg Discrepancy for Nonnegative Weights Suffers from the Curse of Dimensionality
items.summary: We study the normalized discrepancy in the Luxemburg norm generated by $Φ(s)=s\log(1+s)$. For arbitrary nonnegative quadrature weights, we prove that the associated information complexity suffers from the curse of dimensionality: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exist constants $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that \[N_{Φ,+}(\varepsilon,d)\ge c_{\varepsilon} d^{-1}(1.07735\ldots)^d \qquad \mbox{for all } d\ge d_0. \] The result therefore also applies to equal-weight quasi-Monte Carlo rules.

items.title: Optimizers for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality
items.summary: The finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality provides an estimate on the Riesz sum of the first $N$ negative eigenvalues of the fractional Schrödinger operator $(-Δ)^s-V$ in terms of the $L^{γ+\frac{d}{2s}}(\mathbb R^d)$ norm of the potential $V$, where the Riesz exponent $γ>\max\left\{0,1-d/(2s)\right\}$. We prove the existence of optimizers for every finite rank by establishing a result on the spectrum in the case of dichotomy. We further characterize the spectral gap and qualitative properties of optimizers, including the Euler--Lagrange equation, regularity, and asymptotic behavior at infinity. In particular, under the condition $γ+{d}/{(2s)}\geq 3+{4s}/{d}$, we show that all normalized maximizing sequences are precompact modulo translations. Moreover, we derive a strict binding inequality for the optimal constants in the finite-rank setting, which implies that the optimal fractional Lieb--Thirring constant, if it exists, cannot be attained by a potential with finitely many negative eigenvalues.

items.title: Recovery of coefficients in a Schrödinger system with nonlinear coupling
items.summary: We consider the inverse problem of recovering time-dependent coefficients in a system of Schrödinger equations with coupled nonlinear terms. We first address the well-posedness of the system for small boundary data and trivial initial data. Then, we show that the linearized Neumann data stably determines the nonlinear coefficients provided that, at any given time, they are known in some neighborhood of the boundary. The proof relies on linearization and complex geometric optics (CGO) solutions for the linear Schrödinger equation. We conclude by outlining an approach based on the direct use of Carleman estimates to recover time-independent coefficients in the setting of trivial boundary data but nontrivial initial data.

items.title: Almost $L^\infty$-stability of the Ritz projection for the integral fractional Laplacian with $0<s\leq \tfrac12$
items.summary: For $0<s\leq 1/2$ and $d\geq 1$, the $\widetilde H^s$-projection onto piecewise linear finite element spaces on quasi-uniform meshes of a bounded Lipschitz domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a uniform exterior ball condition is almost stable in the maximum norm. The mesh domain need not coincide with the original domain.

items.title: A proof of the interlacing conjecture for the singular values of Sylvester-Kac matrices
items.summary: Boros and Rózsa (Linear Algebra Appl. 421 (2007) 407--416) reduced the singular value problem for the odd-order Sylvester--Kac matrix $P\in\mathbb{R}^{(2m+1)\times(2m+1)}$ to those for $Q^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{(m+1)\times m}$ and $S^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times(m+1)}$ via a permutation similarity transformation. They noted that $(Q^{(m)})^{T}Q^{(m)}-S^{(m)}(S^{(m)})^{T}$ is positive definite, and also conjectured that $σ_i(S^{(m)})\geσ_{i+1}(Q^{(m)})$ for $1\le i\le m-1$ and $m\ge2$. In this paper, we prove that these inequalities are strict and establish the strict interlacing relation \begin{equation*} σ_1(Q^{(m)})>σ_1(S^{(m)})> \cdots>σ_m(Q^{(m)})> σ_m(S^{(m)})>0 \end{equation*} for all $m\ge1$. Here, $σ_i(\cdot)$ denotes the $i$-th largest singular value of a matrix.

items.title: Non-symmetric vector dyson equations
items.summary: We study the vector Dyson equation $$-\frac{1}{m(z)}=z\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{a}+Sm(z),$$ with parameter $z$ in the complex upper half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+$, where $\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^d$ and $S$ is a nonnegative matrix, not necessarily symmetric. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. We also obtain the corresponding estimates for symmetric matrices in the periodic setting.

items.title: Second Maximum of a Gaussian Random Field and Exact (t-)Spacing test
items.summary: In this article, we introduce the novel concept of the second maximum of a Gaussian random field defined on a Riemannian manifold: Once the field reaches its global maximum at a point $t_1$, the second maximum is the largest value of the field away from $t_1$, after the value and the gradient of the field at $t_1$ have been removed. This statistic serves as a powerful tool for characterizing the distribution of the global maximum. By employing an ad-hoc Kac-Rice formula, we derive the explicit distribution of the maximum, conditioned on the second maximum and the independent part of the Riemannian Hessian (the part of the Hessian at $t_1$ that is independent of the value and the gradient of the field at $t_1$). This approach yields an exact test based on the spacing between these maxima, which we refer to as the spacing test. We investigate the applicability of this test for detecting sparse alternatives in Gaussian symmetric tensors, continuous sparse deconvolution, and two-layered neural networks with smooth rectifiers. Theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments that illustrate the calibration and power of the proposed procedures. More generally, we provide a framework for applying the spacing test to continuous sparse regression for any Gaussian random field on a Riemannian manifold. Furthermore, when the variance-covariance function is known only up to a scaling factor, we derive an exact Studentized version of the procedure, coined the t-spacing test. We show that this test is perfectly calibrated under the null hypothesis and exhibits high power for detecting sparse alternatives. As a corollary, we derive an exact, non-asymptotic test for the spiked tensor model without requiring prior knowledge of the noise level.

items.title: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic $(L_0, L_1)$-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
items.summary: We study the stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) complexity of finding $ε$-stationary points of $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth nonconvex functions. Under bounded-variance noise, existing analyses of normalized and clipped stochastic gradient descent (SGD) establish optimal dependence on $ε$ and $L_0$, but the jointly optimal dependence on $L_0$, $L_1$, and $ε$ remains unclear. We resolve this question for an unbiased SFO whose gradient noise has a $p$th central moment bounded by $σ^p$ for some $σ\geq 0$, where $p\in(1,2]$.Specifically, we establish an SFO lower bound of $Ω\big(\big(σ^{\frac{p}{p-1}}ε^{-\frac{p}{p-1}}+1\big) (L_0 Δε^{-2}+L_1Δε^{-1})\big)$, where $Δ>0$ is the initial optimality gap.This bound identifies an unavoidable contribution proportional to $L_1ε^{-1}Δ$. We also prove that mini-batch (smoothed) normalized SGD can attain a matching upper bound, thereby establishing the optimal SFO complexity.

items.title: Boundary Harnack inequalities for the fractional $p$-Laplacian in Reifenberg flat domains
items.summary: We prove a scale-invariant boundary Harnack inequality and Hölder continuity up to the boundary of quotients of positive fractional $p$-harmonic functions in Reifenberg flat domains with sufficiently small flatness constant, for $0<s<1$ and $2\le p<2/(1-s)$. The solutions are globally nonnegative, vanish on a common exterior boundary patch, and belong to the natural local energy and $(p-1)$-tail class. Their distant exterior values may be unrelated and unbounded. After normalization at a corkscrew point, the comparison and Hölder constants depend only on $n,s,p$. We first establish local half-space boundary comparison for every $p\ge2$ and prove relative approximation by the half-space profile in Reifenberg domains. The compactness argument identifies escaped exterior mass and excludes its constant source term. Interior $C^{1,α}$ regularity then yields gradient non-degeneracy and lower increment bounds in a cone of directions. To treat the degenerate kernels produced by linearization, we develop estimates for weighted non-local forms and prove a localized Harnack inequality for bounded quotients, retaining the full exterior interactions. Ordered variational deformations and a common fractional $p$-harmonic majorant yield comparison for solutions with unrelated exterior data. Truncation of distant data and fractional $p$-harmonic replacement extend the estimates from the variational energy class to the natural tail class.

items.title: Projection-Based Parareal for Nonlinear Initial-Value Problems
items.summary: Parareal is a parallel-in-time method for initial-value problems that has found extensive applications and given rise to many variants. Krylov-enhanced parareal is a variant of parareal that uses projection techniques to accelerate convergence substantially for linear problems. In this paper, we study a projection-based parareal algorithm for nonlinear initial-value problems with a modified iteration scheme and an arbitrary orthogonal projection. For a general nonlinear problem, we prove a convergence estimate for each iteration step on a fixed time grid. We analyze the errors of the modified scheme and the scheme of Krylov-enhanced parareal relative to the old error as the coarse grid is refined. For a coarse solver of order $p$ and step size $h$, we prove error bounds of $O(h^{p+1})$ for the modified scheme and $O(h)$ for that of Krylov-enhanced parareal at the first potentially inexact time point under mild assumptions. Numerical experiments on two nonlinear problems are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

items.title: Contact Blow-up Analysis of the Legendrian Mean Curvature Flow and a Smale-type Theorem for Strict Contactomorphisms of Sasakian Spheres
items.summary: We study the Legendrian mean curvature flow in $η$-Einstein Sasakian manifolds by parabolic rescalings which preserve the contact structure. In a compact $η$-Einstein Sasakian manifold, regular or not, the contact tangent flows at a Type I singularity are, up to vertical translations of their components, self-similar flows of Legendrian self-shrinkers in the Heisenberg group, and they are unions of Legendrian planes. When the Reeb orbits are not closed, as on the irregular Sasaki--Einstein manifolds, the leaf space of the Reeb foliation is not a Kähler manifold or orbifold, and this result does not follow by projecting the flow to a Lagrangian mean curvature flow; its proof combines local transverse estimates with a Gaussian density localised in a flow box of the Reeb foliation. In a regular manifold a Type I singularity can only form at a point of transverse Gaussian density at least $2$. We apply the analysis to strict contactomorphisms $\varphi$ of the standard Sasakian sphere $\mathbb S^{2k+1}$, whose Legendrian graphs lie in the $η$-Einstein manifold $(\mathbb S^{2k+1}\times\mathbb S^{2k+1})/\mathbb S^1$. The Jacobian of a Legendrian graph obeys a reaction--diffusion equation whose quadratic term is a sum of squares when $k=1$ and is indefinite when $k\geq2$. For every strict contactomorphism of $\mathbb S^3$, and for every pinched strict contactomorphism of $\mathbb S^{2k+1}$, $k\geq2$, the contact blow-ups of the flow of its Legendrian graph are flat, the flow exists for all time and, up to a rotation along the Reeb flow, converges exponentially to the graph of an element of $U(k+1)$. In particular such a $\varphi$ is isotopic to $U(k+1)$ through strict contactomorphisms.

items.title: 3d Super Hyperbolic Geometry
items.summary: Wigner's unitary representation of the Lorentz group is extended to a representation of the complex orthosymplectic Lie supergroup (\operatorname{OSp}_{\mathbb C}(1|2)) acting on Minkowski ((3,1|4))-dimensional superspace essentially by Hermitian conjugation. The invariant quadratic form is[x_1x_2-x\bar x+φψ+\barφ\barψ]in Wigner's real coordinates (x_1,x_2) and complex coordinate (x), where (φ) and (ψ) are Dirac fermions. The extended action is linear in the superspace variables, but not quadratic in the odd group variables, and is described by an explicit even purely imaginary auxiliary parameter defined on the product of the Lie supergroup with its Lie algebra. This extension of Wigner's representation opens the door to the study of geometry in super hyperbolic three-space, initiated here with foundations on super geodesics, triangles, and tetrahedra, together with an analysis of ideal tetrahedra and a discussion of the nonzero fermionic correction to the Schläfli formula. This version includes a corrigendum that does not materially affect the main results, except for the claimed divergence of the volume of an ideal tetrahedron: the earlier divergence computation was correct as a calculation, but was carried out for an incorrect differential form.

items.title: A quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for a large class of unbounded potentials
items.summary: We prove a quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for a broad class of unbounded potentials when the spatial dimension is five or greater. In the final section, we outline the modifications required to extend the main result to the anisotropic case.

items.title: Equivariant $K$-theory as a global localization
items.summary: We establish a global equivariant refinement of the theorem of Snaith that presents the complex $K$-theory spectrum as a localization of the suspension spectrum of $\mathbb C P^\infty$. We prove that the morphism of ultra-commutative global ring spectra from $Σ^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$ that classifies the tautological $U(1)$-representation exhibits the global $K$-theory spectrum as a specific localization, in both the $\infty$-categories of ultra-commutative ring spectra and of commutative global ring spectra. The classes to be inverted are certain representation-graded $U(n)$-equivariant homotopy classes of $Σ^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$, the pre-Bott classes. We also show that for every compact Lie group $G$, the $G$-equivariant $K$-theory spectrum is a telescopic localization of $Σ^\infty_+ B_G U(1)$ by the pre-Bott classes of all unitary $G$-representations.

items.title: Bessel Periods on $U(2,1) \times U(1,1)$, Relative Trace Formula and Non-Vanishing of Central $L$-values
items.summary: In this paper we calculate the asymptotics of the second moment of the Bessel periods associated to certain holomorphic cuspidal representations $(π, π')$ of $U(2,1) \times U(1,1)$ of regular infinity type (averaged over $π$). Using these, we obtain quantitative non-vanishing results for the Rankin-Selberg central $L$-values $L(1/2, π\times π')$, which are of degree twelve over ${\mathbb Q}$, with concomitant difficulty in applying standard methods, especially since we are in a `conductor dropping' situation. We use the relative trace formula, and the orbital integrals are evaluated rather than compared with others. Besides their intrinsic interest, non-vanishing of these critical values also leads, by known results, to deducing certain associated Selmer groups have rank zero.

items.title: An Adaptive Cubic Regularisation Algorithm Based on Interior-Point Methods for Optimization with General Inequality Constraints
items.summary: Nonlinear constrained optimization has a wide range of practical applications. The interior-point method is considered to be one of the most powerful algorithms for solving nonlinear inequality constrained optimization. In this paper, we consider optimization with general inequality constraints and propose an Adaptive Regularisation algorithm using Cubics Based on Interior-Point methods (ARCBIP). For solving the barrier problem, we construct ARC subproblem with linearized constraints and the well-known fraction to the boundary rule that prevents slack variables from approaching their lower bounds prematurely. We employ a composite-step approach and reduced Hessian methods to deal with linearized constraints, where the trial step is decomposed into a normal step and a tangential step. They are obtained by solving two ARC subproblems approximately with the fraction to the boundary rule. Requirements on normal steps and tangential steps are given to ensure global convergence. To determine whether the trial step is accepted, we use exact penalty function as the merit function in ARC framework. The updating of the barrier parameter is implemented by adaptive strategies. Global convergence is analyzed under mild assumptions. Preliminary numerical experiments and some comparison results are reported.

items.title: Local stability of Frobenius and Artin--Schreier base-change: a comparison
items.summary: Let $(X,Δ)\to C$ be a family of pairs over a smooth curve in positive characteristic $p>0$. We study the discrepancies of divisors over the base-change $(X,Δ)\to C$ along Artin--Schreier and Frobenius covers of $C$, through ramification data for Artin--Schreier and degree $p$ purely inseparable extensions of DVRs. As an application, we recover a result of Hu and Zong about permanence of local stability for such base-change.

items.title: A logarithmic Brascamp--Lieb variance inequality
items.summary: We prove a strengthened Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even log-concave measures whose positive sublevel bodies satisfy the local logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequality. The conclusion can be written either by adding a rank-one term to the Hessian of the potential or by adding an explicit nonnegative remainder to the variance. The proof uses sublevel volume variations, a one-dimensional Brascamp--Lieb inequality, and the coarea formula. The derivative of the potential under dilations gives an equality function whenever it is square-integrable. For potentials homogeneous of degree greater than one, we obtain a sharp radial remainder.

items.title: Arithmetic Circuits and Neural Networks for Regular Matroids
items.summary: We prove that there exist uniform $(+,\times,/)$-circuits of size $O(n^3)$ to compute the basis generating polynomial of regular matroids on $n$ elements. By tropicalization, this implies that there exist uniform $(\max,+,-)$-circuits and ReLU neural networks of the same size for weighted basis maximization of regular matroids. As a consequence in linear programming theory, we obtain a first example where taking the difference of two extended formulations can be more efficient than the best known individual extended formulation for the base polytope of regular matroids of size $O(n^6)$ by Aprile and Fiorini. Such differences have recently been introduced as virtual extended formulations. The proof of our main result relies on a fine-tuned version of Seymour's decomposition of regular matroids which allows us to identify and maintain graphic substructures to which we can apply a local version of the star-mesh transformation.

items.title: Matrix-valued regular functions of a quaternionic variable - a decomposition and some approximation results
items.summary: A quaternionic matrix-valued regular function is a map $F: Ω\rightarrow M_n(\mathbb{H})$ whose entries are (left) regular functions of a quaternion variable, where $Ω$ is a domain in $\mathbb{H}$. Given any $n \times n$ matrix-valued regular function $F(q)$ over $\mathbb{H}$ having norm at most $1$, we derive a decomposition of $F(q)$ in the form $U \star \begin{bmatrix} ||F(q_0)|| & 0\\0 & G(q)\end{bmatrix} V$ for some constant unitary matrices $U, V$, some vector $q_0$ and an $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ matrix-valued regular function $G(q)$, where $\star$ denotes the star product over $\mathbb{H}$. We use this to deduce that any matrix-valued regular function $F(q)$ having norm at most $1$ can be uniformly approximated by a convex combination of rational unitary functions.

items.title: Smooth Hard-Thresholding for Singular Values with Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimate
items.summary: Low-rank matrix denoising is a central primitive in patch-based image restoration and many other inverse problems. Classical SVD-based image denoising methods often choose a truncation rank by matching residual singular-value energy with an estimated noise energy, but this rule is not a finite-sample risk principle because a fitted low-rank approximation inevitably absorbs part of the noise. This paper develops a mathematically rigorous alternative based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE). Since singular value hard thresholding is discontinuous and does not satisfy the hypotheses of Stein's lemma, we introduce a logistic smooth hard-threshold spectral estimator. We prove that the smooth shrinker satisfies the regularity conditions required by a spectral-estimator version of Stein's lemma, and therefore admits an exactly unbiased fixed-threshold risk estimate under Gaussian noise. For a fixed observed matrix and a finite set of candidate thresholds separated from the observed singular values, the ordering of the fixed-threshold smooth SURE objective eventually agrees with a simple limiting score. The limiting score has the same algebraic form as the biased hard-threshold SURE formula, but here it is used only as a computational device for ranking finite candidates. Selecting the minimizing threshold is a data-adaptive tuning step; the selected SURE value should not be interpreted as an unbiased risk estimate of the finally selected estimator.

items.title: Data-driven Smooth-to-hard Spectral Regularization for General Linear Inverse Problems
items.summary: The logistic smooth-to-hard shrinker is the proximal map of an explicit saturating spectral penalty for general linear inverse problems. Its exact weak convexity yields a unique scaled update and proximal-gradient stationarity guarantees, while independent validation provides finite-grid parameter-selection control. We use MRI as an illustrative example.

items.title: Automorphisms of triality groups over local rings
items.summary: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative local ring with $2,3\in R^\times$, and let $ρ\in\Aut(R)$ satisfy $ρ^3=\id$. We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full triality groups in the adjoint and simply connected forms of type $D_4$. Every automorphism is uniquely determined by an adjoint group element and a ring automorphism preserving the trace $T=\id+ρ+ρ^2$; conversely, every such pair defines an automorphism. A square-zero example shows that trace-preserving coefficient automorphisms need not normalize $\langleρ\rangle$ when $ρ$ is nontrivial on $R$ but trivial on its residue field. We also prove a relative rigidity theorem for homomorphisms from elementary triality groups over arbitrary coefficient rings to local targets with $2$ and $3$ invertible, assuming that an adjoint conjugation makes the parameter-one root images standard modulo the maximal ideal. Conversely, every unital trace-preserving ring homomorphism into such a local coefficient ring induces the corresponding homomorphism of elementary groups.

items.title: On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins
items.summary: Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For $X \subseteq V(D)$, the inversion of $X$ in $D$ is the oriented graph that is obtained via changing the direction of all edges which have both endpoints in $X$. The inversion number of $D$, $\operatorname{inv}(D)$, is the minimum number of inversions necessary in order to remove all cycles from $D$. A dijoin $D_1 \to D_2$ is the oriented graph obtained by taking disjoint copies of $D_1,D_2$ and adding edges from all $v \in V(D_1)$ to each $u \in V(D_2)$. It was conjectured by Bang-Jensen, da Silva and Havet that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1) + \operatorname{inv}(D_2)$ for all $D_1, D_2$. This was disproved by simultaneous constructions of various $D_1$, $D_2$ with $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2)-1$. However, no known constructions achieved more than this gain of 1. Moreover, all of the constructions exploit a gap of 1 between $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ and the minimum rank of a family of related matrices, a gap that can never be more than 1, suggesting that perhaps something close to the original conjecture might be true. We prove that in fact additivity fails badly. In particular, for all $\varepsilon>0$ we show that there exist tournaments $D_1$, $D_2$ with arbitrarily large inversion numbers such that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2} +\varepsilon\right)(\operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2))$.

items.title: Investigating mixed-integer programming approaches for the $p$-$α$-closest-center problem
items.summary: In this work, we introduce and study the $p$-$α$-closest-center problem ($pα$CCP), which generalizes the $p$-second-center problem, a recently emerged variant of the classical $p$-center problem. In the $pα$CCP, we are given sets of customers and potential facility locations, distances between each customer and potential facility location as well as two integers $p$ and $α$. The goal is to open facilities at $p$ of the potential facility locations, such that the maximum $α$-distance between each customer and the open facilities is minimized. The $α$-distance of a customer is defined as the sum of distances from the customer to its $α$ closest open facilities. If $α$ is one, the $pα$CCP is the $p$-center problem, and for $α$ being two, the $p$-second-center problem is obtained, for which the only existing algorithm in literature is a variable neighborhood search (VNS). We present four mixed-integer programming (MIP) formulations for the $pα$CCP, strengthen them by adding valid and optimality-preserving inequalities and conduct a polyhedral study to prove relationships between their linear programming relaxations. Moreover, we present iterative procedures for lifting some valid inequalities to improve initial lower bounds on the optimal objective function value of the $pα$CCP and characterize the best lower bounds obtainable by this iterative lifting approach. Based on our theoretical findings, we develop a branch-and-cut algorithm (B&C) to solve the $pα$CCP exactly. We improve its performance by a starting and a primal heuristic, variable fixings and separating inequalities. In our computational study, we investigate the effect of the various ingredients of our B&C on benchmark instances from related literature. Our B&C is able to prove optimality for 17 of the 40 instances from the work on the VNS heuristic.

items.title: Inherent Trade-offs when Enforcing Correct Data Symmetries in Multi-head Self-attention
items.summary: We give a complete characterization of equivariant multi-head self-attention (MHSA): if an MHSA layer is equivariant to a symmetry group $G$, then $G$ can only act by permuting head-clusters, with QK and OV matrices satisfying an equivariance constraint tied to the group action. As a consequence, we prove that any fixed MHSA architecture that achieves exact equivariance by polynomially parameterizing unconstrained MHSA parameters inevitably leads to expressivity loss within the class of equivariant maps: the equivariance locus of unconstrained MHSA forms a union of extremely many Zariski-irreducible components in a reduced parameter space, and any single architecture covers at most one. For $G=D_4$ acting on $C$ copies of the regular representation as the token feature space, we show that there are $Ω(C^{64})$ components for eight attention heads. We illustrate this with experiments on artificial tasks and show that the predicted head-cluster structures can arise naturally when the attention layer is pressured to become equivariant.

items.title: Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems II
items.summary: The paper "Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems II" continues the line of "Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems" from the perspective of almost classical localizations of algebras and the conclusions of K.~I.~Beidar's doctoral dissertation. This allows one to apply the orthogonal completion method to describe non-degenerate orthogonally complete algebras bases on known classifications of strongly prime algebras.

items.title: Magnetic uncertainty in variable geometry
items.summary: In this paper, we study Hardy-type uncertainty principles and unique continuation properties for linear covariant Schrodinger equations with variable coefficients in the presence of bounded electric and magnetic potentials. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the leading coefficients, we prove that any solution exhibiting super-quadratic exponential decay at two distinct times must vanish identically. Under an additional structural assumption on the coefficient matrix $G$, we further establish a Hardy-type result at the quadratic exponential scale. We also obtain an analogous uniqueness result for the heat equation with variable-coefficient magnetic perturbations. Our results unify and extend previous works in two directions: they recover the constant-coefficient covariant case treated by Barcelo-Fanelli-Gutierrez-Ruiz-Vilela when $G=I$, and the variable-coefficient non-magnetic case considered by Federico-Li-Yu when $A=0$. The proofs combine logarithmic convexity arguments with Carleman estimates adapted to variable-coefficient covariant Schrödinger and parabolic flows. Although our approach follows the general strategy introduced by Escauriaza-Kenig-Ponce-Vega, substantial new difficulties arise from the interaction between the variable metric and the magnetic structure, which requires new weight functions and refined commutator estimates.

items.title: Algebraic derivations and radicals of automorphism groups of algebras
items.summary: The paper "Algebraic derivations and radicals of automorphism groups of algebras" continues both the well-known line of description of algebraic derivations of semiprime associative algebras in terms of inner derivations of their symmetric Martindale rings of quotients, and results on the coincidence of the prime and weakly solvable radicals of subgroups of multiplicative groups of PI-rings using the example of automorphism groups of algebras associated with their algebraic derivations.

items.title: A prime plus a square: A conditional 11/20 upper bound
items.summary: Let $E_\square(N)$ count the positive integers at most $N$ that cannot be expressed as a prime plus a nonnegative integer square. Assuming that every nontrivial zero of every primitive Dirichlet $L$-function has real part at most $7/8$, we prove $E_\square(N)\ll_\eps N^{11/20+\eps}$ for every $\eps>0$. The proof combines a conductor-weighted mean-square estimate with a uniform estimate for certain families having a prescribed quadratic component. For these families, the large sieve depends on the varying part of the conductor, while an approximate functional equation controls the fourth moment using the full conductor. A zero-detection argument then absorbs all bands of zeros with real part at least $129/167$. The remaining bands and the minor arcs give the exponent $11/20$. The proof includes even denominators, completion and positivity of the singular series, and removal of proper prime powers.

items.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.

items.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
items.summary: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of video generative pretraining for unified 4D perception. See https://gen4p.github.io for more visual results.

items.title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
items.summary: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. Existing method addresses this by preserving prompt-aligned foreground regions, thereby protecting semantically relevant structures. However, this text-relevance criterion overlooks background objects, local details that are not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, leading to degraded structural coherence. In this work, we propose Dynamics-aware Token Merging (DaTMe), a training-free framework that grounds token merging in the underlying diffusion dynamics. Our key insight is that token importance should reflect whether a token remains unresolved during denoising and whether it carries structural information. To this end, DaTMe constructs a dynamics- aware importance map from the Tweedie denoised estimate. The map combines a temporal signal, measuring inter-step changes in the predicted clean image, with a structural signal, capturing local high-frequency content such as boundaries and fine details. Using this map, DaTMe adaptively assigns tokens into merging roles under a given compression ratio: important tokens are preserved as anchors, while tokens that are both temporally stabilized and structurally homogeneous are selected as safe merge candidates. Experiments on PixArt-a and FLUX demonstrate that DaTMe maintains visual fidelity across the entire image, highlighting diffusion dynamics as an effective token-level merging decision in efficient generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/SeungJuCha/DaTMe.

items.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. Dynamic caching methods decide when to refresh by accumulating a cheap probe of the network input into a staleness signal and spending a fresh evaluation once it crosses a threshold. They perform hard caching: the signal is a binary switch between refresh and reuse, and every step, fresh or cached, advances by the prescribed step size. We observe that the signal carries much more than this switch. How far it sits below the threshold, its headroom, predicts the error induced by reuse. We propose SoftCache, which performs soft caching: instead of a binary switch, the headroom sets how far each cached step goes. Where the headroom is large, the sampler jumps past several scheduled nodes, and as a refresh nears, its steps shrink back toward the original step. These adaptive jumps may land between the scheduled nodes, taking the sampler off its fixed grid. SoftCache requires no training and adds no per-backbone settings: on FLUX for images and on HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 for video, at speedups from $3.5\times$ to $6.9\times$, it is ahead of every baseline on all four fidelity metrics.

items.title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies
items.summary: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. We present Value as Memory (VaM), a framework that addresses these challenges through value caching and online real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. Across long-horizon tasks involving deformable objects and contact-rich manipulation, VaM yields a mean absolute success-rate gain of $29.4\%$ with value caching, while achieving a $32.8\%$ gain with online autonomous learning over matched offline training. The evaluated online schedule performs $8\times$ as many policy iterations under the same gradient-step budget, with more than $2\times$ lower recorded time per gradient step with concurrent data collection and training.

items.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
items.summary: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.

items.title: GRASP: Plan-Guided Graph Retrieval with Adaptive Fusion and Reranking on Semi-Structured Knowledge Bases
items.summary: Retrieval over semi-structured knowledge bases (SKBs) must handle both textual descriptions and relational constraints. Text-based retrievers capture the overall semantics of a query but struggle with multi-hop relations, whereas graph-based retrievers follow relational paths precisely but miss the broader meaning. We propose GRASP, a hybrid retriever that learns to fuse the two. A small LLM planner translates the query into an executable graph plan in a single call, its graph ranking is fused with a text ranking, and a fine-tuned reranker reorders the fused candidates. Instead of training the planner to be accurate on its own, we optimize it with reinforcement learning to maximize the gain its graph ranking brings to the fused ranking. On three STaRK benchmarks, GRASP achieves the best results on all metrics, improving the average Hit@1 by 18.6 points over the strongest baseline, while taking only 2.47 seconds per query.

items.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
items.summary: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

items.title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets, while producing goal-directed manipulation videos with stronger instruction adherence and action progression than video-generation baselines. Project Page: https://p3-wam.pages.dev/

items.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
items.summary: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.

items.title: Grounding Generative Verification in 3D Content
items.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and 3D generation have expanded 3D understanding and synthesis. However, beyond visual fidelity, task-specific correctness grounded in 3D evidence remains a major challenge. We argue that building reliable 3D systems requires not only stronger generation and reasoning, but also verification feedback that identifies unmet requirements and explains their violations, allowing systems to reflect on and refine their outputs. Such feedback must integrate multi-view observations and distinguish genuine inconsistencies from projection-dependent appearances. We make three contributions. First, we introduce 3DVerifierBench, a benchmark spanning 10 tasks that evaluates decisions, rejection explanations, and responses to controlled changes in specifications and candidates. A human study reveals a 21.6 percentage-point gap between humans and the strongest tested model, GPT-6 Astra, while explanation-aware analysis exposes weaknesses in rejection reliability. Second, we analyze verification across fine-grained factual categories, exposing errors in values and target binding. We develop a scalable pipeline combining multi-view fact extraction, controlled 3D editing, and native annotations to produce 14,126 training examples with contradiction explanations and linked counterfactuals. Third, we examine how verification could support 3D generation through candidate selection and recursive refinement. In human-labeled sixteen-candidate pools, oracle selection improves complete factual success from 26.7% to 90.0%. In a separate eight-input study, human-guided recursive refinement satisfies all seven requirements for every input, compared with three under parallel Oracle@8. Together, our benchmark, analysis, and data pipeline establish a foundation for models to reflect on 3D content through reliable verification feedback.

items.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
items.summary: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws. Together, these enable PathFM to generate multiple paths for a single series in roughly the time needed for one query to a quantile model. The distilled sampler also makes it practical to optimize a calibration loss directly. PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on the established forecasting benchmarks fev-bench and TIME. To complement these evaluations, we introduce Forecast Path Score Bench (fps-bench), which augments fev-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics. PathFM achieves a higher aggregate path score on fps-bench than all evaluated external baselines. Experiments on chaotic systems further show that our flow model sustains long-run variability, while strong baselines rapidly collapse. PathFM makes generative time series forecasting both competitive and practical, enabling diverse downstream applications.

items.title: DK-VLM: Geometry as Position for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models still struggle to understand 3D spatial relations across views and update spatial judgments as the observer moves. A common approach fuses 3D reconstruction features into visual tokens, but aligning these features with pretrained semantic representations remains challenging under limited spatial supervision. We propose DK-VLM with Dual-Kernel Attention, which computes attention from both a visual token's input position and its geometric position in the scene. A semantic kernel retains the pretrained model's native attention and positional encoding, while a separate geometric kernel uses estimated 3D points and camera poses to directly modulate attention through point displacements and relative view transformations. Then, a learned gate fuses their outputs. Geometry thus enters attention as position rather than as fused reconstruction features. We further introduce Reference-Frame Composition (RC) supervision to train the model to update its reference frame across successive judgments. It provides stepwise turn and heading targets derived from verified single-step annotations. Among the compared methods, DK-VLM-8B achieves the highest average score across six spatial benchmarks and the highest overall scores on VSI-Bench (74.33) and ReVSI-32 (58.28). RC supervision further improves multi-step spatial reasoning, while the full model preserves general video understanding. Project page: https://sumuru789.github.io/DK-VLM-website/.

items.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
items.summary: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique signal. Our experiments further demonstrate that these structured and interpretable outputs improve the verifier's generalization to out-of-domain multimodal critic tasks. To train this verifier, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise local feedback to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable continuous scoring at the global level. Under a general reinforcement learning framework, we first empirically demonstrate that the proposed pointwise graded verifier significantly outperforms binary verifiers in traditional text-to-image scenarios. We then extend our investigation to rule-governed generative world modeling where generative models are leveraged for world simulation and world reasoning under explicit rules. From a theoretical standpoint, we further show that a pairwise verification paradigm yields more accurate critiques than the pointwise formulation when ground-truth images are available, with empirical results on diverse structured world-modeling tasks such as Maze and Sudoku further validating the effectiveness of our approach. Overall, our findings suggest a key insight: the transition from generative models to structured world-modeling agents critically hinges on the availability of accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers.

items.title: Scaling Multilingual Mixture-of-Experts: How Language Coverage Changes Capacity and Compute Allocation
items.summary: Multilingual models share capacity across languages, so adding languages can hurt performance on existing ones. Mixture-of-experts models expand this capacity with little additional per-token computation. Given this extra capacity, does adding experts reduce what each additional language costs? To answer this question, we propose a repetition-aware joint scaling law relating number of active parameters, training tokens per language, number of experts, and language coverage. Fitted on 26,300 per-language loss observations from 64 pretrained configurations, our law reduces prediction error on held-out configurations by 28% relative to the strongest evaluated baseline. At matched number of active parameters and training tokens per language, 32 experts reduce the loss penalty of expanding from 12 to 200 languages by 83% compared with a dense model. Our law further shows that broader language coverage favors more experts across a wider range of compute budgets, guiding capacity allocation as multilingual models scale.

items.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
items.summary: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models have become an important approach for scaling model parameters. Modern MoE architectures increasingly combine two design choices: fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts. The former increases expressiveness by enabling more expert combinations at a fixed activation ratio, and the latter introduces experts that are active for every token. We identify an exploration dilemma between these designs: shared experts can make routing less exploratory by reducing the variability of token representations. This conflicts with the greater need for exploration induced by fine-grained expert segmentation due to the combinatorially enlarged routing space. Consequently, the additional expressiveness offered by fine-grained segmentation may not be fully realized in practice. MirrorMoE is proposed to reconcile this exploration dilemma by shrinking the exploration space through token-adaptive suppression of unnecessary experts. MirrorMoE consistently improves performance across model scales.

items.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
items.summary: Single image 3D generation aims to dress a given 3D mesh with relightable materials while faithfully preserving the visual details of a reference image. Existing methods either introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or struggle to preserve fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning. To resolve these challenges, we introduce SUPRA-Tex, built on the principle of decoupling visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion. This division of labor allows the 3D generator, trained on limited 3D data, to focus its capacity on preserving visible evidence and completing unobserved surfaces. Specifically, we first train an MLLM-based image editing model to predict lighting-separated PBR maps in the reference view. We then project these maps onto the visible surface and encode them with the pretrained material VAE encoder into native observation latents that share the generation target's latent space. An interleaved flow transformer holds these latents as fixed, read-only anchors while alternating unobserved-region and full-surface updates to generate complete material latents. This design achieves super-alignment with the reference, delivering What You See Is What You Get fidelity on visible regions and coherent completion on unobserved surfaces. Trained solely on public datasets, SUPRA-Tex achieves SOTA performance in both geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end asset generation, matching or even exceeding leading commercial systems on in-the-wild images. Project page: https://supra-3d.github.io/supratex/

items.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
items.summary: Existing agent benchmarks typically evaluate agents on well-specified tasks defined by issue reports, specifications, or task tickets. Real-world customer delivery is different: forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must clarify ambiguous requirements, work in live systems, and uncover unstated constraints. We introduce FDE-Gym, a benchmark of 95 end-to-end delivery tasks from 20 customer scenarios across 18 sectors, each adapted by industry experts from real-world delivery projects. In simulated customer environments with scripted stakeholders and modifiable customer systems, agents interact with stakeholders and operate on production-like systems to deliver working solutions. FDE-Gym scores a delivery by how much it improves the customer's own success metric, normalized between 0 (unchanged system) and 1 (reference solution), with penalties for stakeholder interactions (messages, trial runs, and waiting time). An online platform lets humans practice FDE skills under the same grading criteria. We evaluate 13 model configurations from seven providers. In the realistic setting, where unstated constraints must be discovered, the best configuration achieves a mean FDE-Gym score of 0.56 and resolves only 14 of the 95 tasks (a score of at least 0.8 with no incident). Discovering unstated constraints is the primary bottleneck: performance drops sharply when models must uncover them without explicit guidance. Yet information discovery alone does not account for the gap: even on the 23 tasks where the best configuration obtains every key fact from stakeholders, it reaches a normalized business uplift of 0.8 or above on only 10. These results reveal a substantial gap between solving well-specified tasks and delivering effective AI systems for real customers.

items.title: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
items.summary: Few-step autoregressive video generators enable streaming generation, yet they run every token through the final denoising step, regardless of how much refinement it needs. We find this uniform computation is often unnecessary: many tokens already closely match their eventual full-step outputs in the initial steps, while others require refinement until the end. We introduce Speculative Forcing, a framework that treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts when individual tokens can be safely accepted early. Once accepted, a token is frozen as its final output and undergoes no further denoising, while its cached keys and values remain available as context for the remaining tokens. We explore two alternative verifier designs: a training-free one based on similarity to clean content and stability across steps, and a learned one that reads the frozen generator's intermediate features to estimate each token's remaining gap to its full-step output. Across short-video, long-video, and world generation, Speculative Forcing preserves the quality of full-step sampling while substantially reducing computation. On LongLive, it matches the four-step generator with ~1.7 denoising steps per token, running over 1.5x faster at 41.7 and 37.8 fps. On Lingbot-World 2.0, where camera motion continually changes the visible content, it maintains quality with ~2.5 denoising steps per token and runs 1.35x faster at 24.5 fps.

items.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.

items.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
items.summary: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-frame scale alignment. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and generalizes zero-shot to KITTI and nuScenes. Project page: https://hongchang-liu.github.io/GeoState-project-page/

items.title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: Generalist robot policies benefit from large-scale visual pretraining but often struggle with contact-rich dexterous manipulation, where force, compliance, and incipient slip are hard to observe from images. We present Spark-0, a spatially aligned vision-tactile-language-action (VTLA) model that uses touch in two complementary ways. During pretraining, image-space contact maps derived from tactile gloves, together with features from a frozen 3D geometry teacher, supervise the visual tokens; these objectives are removed at inference. In parallel, a tactile pathway encodes regional force histories and 3D taxel states to condition the action expert. A single checkpoint therefore supports both vision-only and tactile-conditioned deployment. To scale this supervision, we build HumanTouch, a 1,000-hour dataset of full-hand tactile human manipulation, and pretrain Spark-0 on it together with egocentric video, robot data, and simulation. We also release SparkArena, which pairs vision-only simulated tasks with tactile-conditioned real-robot tasks on one dexterous embodiment. Spark-0 achieves the highest mean success rate on both SparkArena tracks and ranks first on all eight aggregate metrics of the Ego Humanoid Manipulation Benchmark. Compared with vision-only pretraining on the same data and compute with touch discarded, retaining the touch of 1,000 hours of HumanTouch raises vision-only success on Ego Humanoid from 52.5% to 71.7%, and success on SparkArena-Real, where touch is also used at deployment, from 44.0% to 52.0%, indicating that touch serves not only as a policy input but also as scalable supervision for dexterous visuomotor pretraining. The Website is available at: https://xsparkai.com/Spark-0.

items.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
items.summary: We introduce 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem that enables coding agents to create editable and verifiable 3D content at scale. 3DCodeVerse comprises large-scale, high-quality datasets of executable 3D code, a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, and practical guidance for 3D coding. First, we construct 3DCodeVerse-2M, a large-scale curated dataset of standalone 3D executable code. We build this corpus by collecting open-source data, converting specialized representations, and generating new programs with coding agents. Each program is packaged with the source files and associated assets required for execution in its declared environment, along with available descriptions and verification records. Second, we develop the 3DCodeVerse Harness, a multi-agent directed acyclic graph framework for generating and refining 3D content. It uses execution checks, spatial measurements, and visual feedback to automatically evaluate and revise generated programs without human feedback during generation. Third, we conduct systematic empirical studies of 3D coding, establishing baselines with fine-tuned open models and deriving practical guidance through component-level analyses of our harness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that fine-tuning on our dataset significantly improves the 3D coding capabilities of open-source models. Notably, our 3DCodeVerse harness achieves a 90% win rate against Claude Design (3D Object) in pairwise human evaluations, when both are utilized by Claude Opus 5.5.

items.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
items.summary: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. During inference, the same play policy then guides model-predictive control (MPC) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed-loop, goal-conditioned policy through self-play within the learned world model. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.

items.title: EmbodiedMidtrain: Bridging the Gap between Vision-Language Models and Vision-Language-Action Models via Mid-training
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) inherit their visual and linguistic capabilities from Vision-Language Models (VLMs), yet most VLAs are built from off-the-shelf VLMs that are not adapted to the embodied domain, limiting their downstream performance. In this work, we propose EmbodiedMidtrain to bridge the gap between VLMs and VLAs. We first characterize the data distribution gap between them, showing that VLA data occupy compact regions that are largely separated from the broader VLM distribution, while the degree of alignment varies substantially both across and within VLM data sources. Then, we build a mid-training data engine that leverages a lightweight learnable proximity estimator to select the most VLA-aligned candidates from a large VLM pool, and produce EmbodiedMidtrain-1M, a VLM dataset that we further use to mid-train the VLM before downstream VLA fine-tuning. Experiments on both simulated robot manipulation benchmarks and real-world tasks show consistent VLA performance gains over off-the-shelf checkpoints across VLM backbones and VLA action heads. These gains extend to downstream tasks not used to guide data selection. Further analysis reveals that mid-training provides a stronger initialization for VLA fine-tuning, with gains emerging from the earliest steps and widening throughout training. Moreover, the data engine captures both dataset-level and sample-level alignment signals, favoring spatial reasoning over text-centric tasks while preserving the diversity of the VLM data. We will release all code, data and models for future research.

items.title: Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving
items.summary: Retrieving relevant lemmas is crucial for formal theorem proving, enabling provers to build machine-checkable proofs from established mathematical results. Recent retrieval systems match library declarations to a target theorem or its intermediate proof steps, but make limited use of multi-hop dependencies among declarations. These dependencies can reveal supporting lemmas that are not necessarily lexically similar to the target theorem but recur in proofs of related problems. To this end, we propose LeanGraphSearch, a graph-based retrieval method for Lean 4 that constructs a graph from Mathlib's forward dependencies and traverses it to uncover supporting lemmas through multi-hop dependency chains. Specifically, LeanGraphSearch links each declaration to the premises it depends on, uses a graph-based ranking algorithm to propagate relevance from semantically matched declarations to their dependencies, and reranks the expanded candidates against the original query. Across two mathematical retrieval benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves recall by up to 12% over the strongest baseline, LeanSearch v2, on MathlibQR and increases coverage of complete annotated proof routes on MathlibMPR, covering up to 3.7% of extra groups. More importantly, we evaluate whether these retrieval gains translate into improved end-to-end theorem proving by integrating LeanGraphSearch into an iterative proving loop guided by Lean feedback. Across three theorem proving benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves pass rate at {8, 16, 32} reflection turns by as much as 40% compared to vanilla prover and at most 10% compared to LeanSearch v2, showing higher accuracy-cost efficiency. These findings highlight the value of dependency graph search for theorem proving and motivate further research on structure-aware search for proof discovery.

items.title: Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Path-Safe Target Reaching in Robotic Harvesting of Hydroponic Lettuce
items.summary: Robotic harvesting requires precise manipulation to ensure accurate positioning of the end-effector, especially in a constraint workspace. This study introduces the Path-Safe Approach Proximal Policy Optimization (PSA-PPO), a target-conditioned local reaching framework designed for robotic harvesting of nutrient film technique (NFT)-hydroponic lettuce in greenhouses.
